### a

# Part A: evidence and continuing attacks

## Main fixed-element result

A.1 is proved by reducing to the local closed commutator subgroup, not by
reassembling maximal pro-prime quotients. The key primary source is
Mochizuki--Tsujimura, *Resolution of Nonsingularities, Point-theoreticity,
and Metric-admissibility for p-adic Hyperbolic Curves*, 30 March 2024,
Theorem A, Definition 2.2(i), Proposition 2.3(v),(ix), Proposition 2.4(vii).
The statement on printed pp.51--52 and proof p.54 were opened and read.
The uniqueness clause does not have the extra open cyclotomic-image
hypothesis of its existence clause. The proof of A.1 supplies existence
using the specified point or cusp. A second agent independently checked
the primary theorem's hypotheses before the statement was marked Proved.

For a local field of residue cardinality q, the closed commutator subgroup
maps onto a subgroup containing (q-1)Z_r in tame inertia for every r
different from the residue characteristic. It is contained in the local
intersection with the global abelian-field kernel. Thus the passage from
the local cyclotomic kernel to this smaller kernel loses none of the
uniqueness hypothesis needed here. It does lose open cyclotomic image,
which prevents use of the existence clause for an arbitrary section.

A.6 computes actual cocycles and the four geometric conjugacy classes of
sections agreeing on Delta. A.9 also decides the existence of a fixed lift
of any pro-prime fixed element of an open covering group: it must be in
the image of the actual specified inertia. This does not claim that fixed
points commute with taking quotients.

## Primary-source checks

Nakamura 1994: Theorem 2.1.1 and Lemma 2.1.2 were opened in the publisher
PDF. The former's normalizer condition is an actual cyclotomic action on
the generated subgroup. The latter explicitly allows every nonidentity
element of a free factor, including an exponent supported at one prime.
This confirms the source step of LM8 G.19/R3, conditional on its already
separate pro-prime input. Nakamura 1995: Claim 4.14.1, equation 4.14.2 and
Corollary 4.15 were opened. Tsunogai 1995 was opened at the publisher.
These pro-prime results are not needed for A.1's proof.

## Normalized-procyclic question: current attack

The full normalizer question is separate from A.1: the normalizer need
not contain an arithmetic section. The configuration in LM6 A.62 has
geometric kernel P times C, with P pro-l and C pro-prime-to-l. A pro-l
Sylow subgroup over a pro-l local Galois subgroup gives a splitting
through C. At a place of residue characteristic p different from l,
the local pro-l subgroup has tame Z_l and open l-cyclotomic image, so
the existence clause of MT Proposition 2.4(vii) produces a primitive
valuation. At a good place, the action on P is unramified; uniqueness
for tame inertia then puts P in its geometric stabilizer. The remaining
step is to control this stabilizer well enough to force horizontal cusp
inertia. A primitive valuation need not already be horizontal. This step
is not established, and is not inferred from A.1.

### a_normalizer_fifth_hour

# Full-normalizer attempts during the fifth hour

These attempts address A.2/A.7 and yield no additional claimed theorem. The exact surviving configuration remains A.17: N0=P semidirect B, geometric kernel P times C, P=Z_l, C pro-prime-to-l, and B onto G_L. The actual quotient N0/C splits; lifting that section through C is the unresolved step.

## Cohomological dimension and local duality

A local full arithmetic group of an affine curve has geometric cohomological dimension one and arithmetic dimension two. A normalizer with a geometric procyclic l-component can therefore still have l-dimension three; dimension alone does not contradict the embedding. Proper compactification gives a duality group of dimension four, where a dimension-three subgroup is also not excluded. An infinite-index dimension drop available for certain Poincaré duality groups cannot be applied to the affine free-geometric extension as if it were a Poincaré duality group. No useful top-degree restriction map has been proved injective.

## Splitting over smaller Galois groups

Restricting to the abelian-closure Galois group, or to a suitable local l-Sylow subgroup, can remove a prime-complement obstruction and produce a section over an infinite algebraic extension. It does not produce a section over a finite local number field. The known local section input cannot be invoked for the former as if it were the latter. Likewise A.1 concerns a specified cusp packet; a newly constructed arbitrary section over Delta has not been shown to belong to such a packet.

## Geometric centralizers and Hall arguments

A free profinite group need not have procyclic centralizers of arbitrary pro-l elements. Groups of the form Z_l times a free pro-q group, q different from l, are compatible with projectivity; the special procyclic centralizer theorem for actual cusp inertia cannot be used for an unidentified P. Nor does the discrete Hall free-factor theorem automatically give a finite-index free factor containing an arbitrary closed profinite procyclic subgroup. We have supplied no proof of such a reduction.

## Primary-source search

The renewed searches for procyclic arithmetic normalizers, cuspidal recognition, and Nakamura's weight criterion led again to the cyclotomic-normalizer recognition theorem and its exposition in Stix, not to a theorem that every arithmetic normalizer acts cyclotomically. A.16 already isolates the remaining CM weight-one possibility. The arithmetic weight-one detection in finite proper covers is not sufficient to annul the prime-complement extension in the actual full group.

These failures have not been converted into counterexamples: an abstract nonsplit extension remains distinct from a subgroup embedded in the given arithmetic fundamental group.

## Sixth-hour check against the stronger local formation theorem

D.54/D.56 do not remove the prime-complement embedding problem. Projecting to one coefficient prime kills the complementary geometric kernel but gives a one-prime quotient, to which the two-prime local theorem does not apply. Retaining the residue prime in a full formation also retains a potentially nontrivial part of that kernel; the actual section has still not been constructed. Restriction to a local pro-ell Sylow at residue characteristic p different from ell does satisfy the inertia-surjection and open cyclotomic-image hypotheses of Mochizuki--Tsujimura Theorem F(i), reopened at printedpp7--8. It supplies a unique compatible Berkovich point, as already recorded above. The fixed constant field is then an infinite algebraic extension of a local field, however, and D.56 and Hoshi's local birational proposition have not been proved in that enlarged scope. Thus this revisited route still stops at a vertical stabilizer, without a horizontal point or a finite-local-field section.

A.80 constructs and treats the actual natural degree-eight genus-two intermediate of the order-64 wreath closure C2 wreath C4. The previous cyclic-derived families do not contain this closure. The equations define the double cover, its cyclic four-isogeny and both actual elliptic quotients. The four translated Kummer classes are proved independent through the nontrivial half-divisor class of their norm. Exact programs check the finite permutation group, rational map identities, quotient equations and complete finite-field point counts.

The complementary elliptic factor is non-CM: two ordinary reductions have distinct geometric quadratic endomorphism fields. The proof uses those exact fields and specialization, not a numerical j approximation. At residue characteristic two, the actual closure gives potential good Jacobian reduction and zero two-rank. Every proper stable genus-two configuration is checked. The remaining degree-(2,0) case can put a cusp on a contracted positive-genus tail, so zero rank alone does not furnish a rational companion path.

The new all-weight argument removes the main elliptic handles while retaining every individual Prym handle in the coefficient algebra. Its top slot operator is multiplication by a nonzero polynomial whose coefficient sum is the positive distance from the main component to the chosen cusp path. This proves injectivity in every weight. The actual non-CM Prym supplies SL2, making the surviving invariant grades scalar Tate. The actual-subgroup criterion then returns to integral fixed inertia. Its normal closure is constructed as the compositum of translated quadratic fields. The proper-model, marked-path and global-to-local block comparisons are checked anew. In particular the fixed A.80 curve gives an unbounded family under the isogenies [2^r] eta, with degree 2 times 4^(r+1) and two fewer cusps. Each is treated as its actual cover. ## Exact outer derived depth and finite framed characters

C.48 proves the required centralizer theorem in the actual free prosolvable quotients, using the integral completed relation module and an invariant-measure argument at every prime. A normalized multiplier-one automorphism that is inner at derived depth d has its retained conjugator in the dth derived subgroup. Abelianization handles arbitrary multipliers. Together with the actual C.46 witness and C.47 upper bound, this proves that four is the least derived depth detecting the full parity character in the outer action. Compactness supplies a finite characteristic outer detector at that depth. No minimal finite size is inferred.

C.49 computes the actual multiplier-one retained-frame images at the requested levels 24 and 60. Their orders are 96 and 2880, and their arithmetic images have orders 48 and 1440. The exact genuine sign and local norm-lifting conditions are retained; a residue norm equation alone is not treated as an adelic lifting theorem. The additional level-five shear comes from the actual Tate parameter and arithmetic Kummer character, with an independent C5 in the kernel of the paired CM image. Thus the arithmetic subgroup is exactly the parity kernel at both levels, and the only nontrivial arithmetic-trivial finite-order character coming from these frames is Delta.

The added full-group consequence is explicitly conditional on the restriction to the multiplier-one subgroup factoring through one of these computed frames. Subtracting its possible Delta restriction leaves a character of the multiplier quotient, and arithmetic multiplier surjectivity kills that character. This does not compute the arbitrary-multiplier framed images or the unrestricted character group.

C.50 constructs an explicit finite fully characteristic outer detector for multiplier one, of derived length at most five and order involving only primes two and three. Its two peripheral coset modules force each centralizer projection into the corresponding cyclic subgroup. The universal first envelope has abelianization (Z/exp(L)) squared; this is proved without assuming an element of L has its full exponent. An inner normalized action therefore has trivial retained conjugator residue. ## Anti-Prym and component argument

The unital actual deck action on the anti-factor has r^n=-1, giving the field Q(zeta_(2n)). Its tensor at2 is a field of degree n. On a nonzero special étale2-Tate space the action is unital, so its dimension is a multiple of n. Since the anti-factor dimension is n, its special rank is either0 or n. In the ordinary alternative, exchanged positive-genus components would produce isogenous invariant and anti-invariant diagonal factors, contradicting invariant rank0 versus ordinary anti-rank. Components with trivial involution are correctly left in the invariant factor. On each nontrivial fixed component, the actual pullback/norm comparison gives quotient rank0. ## Integral and topological checks written in the draft

- The peripheral line is primitive in integral homology. Boundary modulo that line is torsion-free; there are at least three geometric cusp directions, and any two have zero intersection.

## Verified established inputs and their exact scopes

- **verified:** D83 gives the actual global and local operator subgroups for every closed away-five lattice, before imposing its local-generator equality. Its uniformly convergent Kummer cochains and one integral gauge in the lattice apply to infinite support. The present proof uses exactly those formulas.
- **verified:** D82 proves that the actual Kummer cocycle of five factors through the untwisted image, that the quotient by its joint kernel with the cyclotomic character is the full affine group, and that the joint kernel contains an actual cubic-primitive element. The raw moment normalization is Nakamura–Sakugawa–Wojtkowiak equations(1.1)–(1.2), <https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1045>, independently opened in the D82 audits. No new higher-weight extension or formal replacement action is assumed.
- **verified:** D78/D81 establish continuous translation coinduction and the actual inclusion of the coefficient invariants. D85 also explains the finite-coset transversal for its open rank-two lattice and why the natural restriction map is the same coefficient inclusion.
- **verified:** D84 computes the rank-one connecting ideal with its actual semilinear action, including the three-jet extension, the exact cyclotomic-power relation inherited from D79, and the natural augmentation-square inclusion at both infinite indices. D85 maps its extra finite-index term to that actual module; it does not compare rational dimensions or choose unrelated invariant identifications.
- **verified:** D77 computes all local/global Cartier invariants, their natural axis maps, and the continuous splitting of the compact kernel. The exact infinite comparison in D85 is written using that same axis quotient.
- **verified:** D43 and D80 give the local discrete Cartier H1 vanishing and a single common finite coefficient level despite arbitrary infinite ramification. Their finite-duality source is Milne ADT I.Corollary2.3, <https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/ADTnot.pdf>. The exceptional primes are finite at the original residual cubic level; no uniform denominator claim is made for all primes separately.
- **verified:** Finite affine Chebotarev descent is the established D78/D83 argument, with the primary theorem Milne CFT V.3.23, <https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/CFT.pdf>. It is applied at a finite coefficient level before taking the filtered union.
- **verified:** D74 computes the whole first-cohomology fibre only once the explicit rational point supplies section existence. D85 asserts no general existence criterion.

## New integral module argument

The only new away-lattice shape is `L=Z5*u + 5^h*Z5*r`, with h positive and u,r an integral basis. In its actual completed group-ring coordinates, the ideal is `(x,g_h)` with `g_h=(1+y)^(5^h)-1`. Modulo y times this ideal, it is exactly `x Z5[[x]] direct-sum Z5*g_h`, and x annihilates the second term. The local relation is `f_lambda(x)+nu*g_h`. The extra cyclic term carries exact compact character chi cubed, hence nontrivial tame character chi squared after the Cartier untwist. Its coinvariants vanish integrally, leaving the actual D84 ideal module.

The natural map at lambda zero and an exact valuation boundary is explicitly the augmentation-square inclusion into the augmentation ideal after the actual axis quotient. The extra cyclic term maps to zero and has zero coinvariants. Thus no comparison of infinite coranks is used.

The nonzero cubic class remains nonzero on the finite cyclic global coefficient quotient: an actual valuation-one, cubic-zero operator has multiplier minus one equal to y times a unit, forcing any hypothetical primitive to be constant. A primitive cubic element in the joint kernel then contradicts it.

## Certificate scope

The supporting program uses monic Groebner reduction over the integers for the ideal `(xy,y*g_h)`. It checks the exact extra-generator character, detects the incorrect character, and checks the coupled local relation including negative exponents after clearing only units. It exhausts all480 ordered residual bases and all five lambda residues, and verifies the local-depth minimum with actual cancellations and infinite values. It also checks the new actual point `t=-799`, its prime factorization, the Smith form of its away lattice, and its exact five-adic logarithm depth. These finite calculations support the new algebra; the proof handles all indices and all infinite limits structurally.

Applied to D.70/D.71, it gives a genuine finite nilpotent obstruction for every other finite-stage class, uniformly away from the cusp class.
- **D.73** closes the one- and two-cusp gap in generic class-two rigidity. For two cusps the linear map to the exterior square of proper homology retains the surface bivector while killing conjugator corrections; passing to the proper class-two fundamental group would incorrectly lose that information. The resulting theorem applies to every affine hyperbolic curve with a rational chosen cusp.

All four statements received full independent proof audits before integration. D.72 and D.73 additionally received a third audit. The checkpoint-ten visual review actually inspected all fifteen assigned final pages and found no layout defect; the exact pages and hashes are in `notes/de_checkpoint10_visual_review.md`.

The remaining barriers are explicit and unchanged. These generic results do not classify every completed tangent parameter, every Alexander-module fibre, or arbitrary full profinite section classes. The first obstructed finite **derived** length and an explicit obstruction cocycle for the nonzero D.20 Fermat families remain unknown; D.72's nilpotent compactness does not answer that mixed-prime question. General arbitrary-twist first-cohomology ranks, the retained compact terms in global second cohomology, and the abstract nonseparated-kernel type for infinite ramification also remain open. The full higher nonmetabelian reading of D.6 and the general relative-pro-five/cubic-twist assertions of D.9 are not relabeled as solved.

The next D.5 attack is an integral operator-ring argument for finite ramification. The finite arithmetic presentation has positive deficiency, while its actual Alexander operators lie in a three-dimensional solvable pro-five Iwasawa ring. Ore clearing may produce integral cocycle families without assuming that growing rational ranks survive an inverse limit. The outstanding proof checks are faithful action, the absence of finite-rank nonzero operators, and descent through the residual C4 action. This remains notes-only until those bridges and the exact primary ring-theoretic inputs are verified.

### de_checkpoint13_progress

# D/E checkpoint13 research progress

## Direct progress on Task D.5

D79–D83 evaluate previously retained compact terms of the actual unrestricted Alexander cohomology. D79 supplies an all-depth exact cyclotomic-power exclusion in the invertible kappa(2),kappa(3) family. D80 carries it to arbitrary infinite ramification under a primitive local unit vector, with finite local duality and one common global coefficient level. D81 removes local primitivity and determines the mixed finite/free compact kernels for all globally independent completed unit pairs. D82 permits arbitrary five-valuations whenever the away-five residual inertia has rank two. Its actual kappa(5) graph and new affine quotient are proved from the primary raw Soulé moment formula; local residual span determines the finite term, and the actual point t=10 has zero compact kernel.

D83 treats a different family, including dependent and nonprimitive pairs: if the closed away-five valuation lattice is generated by its local unit vector, the entire local-five operator image is the full global image. At each finite coefficient level, actual affine Chebotarev descent and local inflation make Sha1 zero; finite duality gives the exact away-five H2 localization isomorphism. It follows that the separated compact kernel is zero. The proof covers uniformly convergent infinite Kummer sums, pure five-valuations, and the actual point t=5.

Each canonical theorem was integrated only after complete root and independent FGH/PBC proof/source audits. D79–D82 exact certificates were executed and independently reproduced; D83 is structural and uses an already certified logarithm residue. Original drafts, source ledgers, outputs, and audit versions remain. No new diagnostic PDF was created.

## Precise remaining barriers

Task D.5 remains Open overall. The general compact term outside the evaluated families, the abstract nonseparated kernel for arbitrary infinite ramification, arbitrary infinitely ramified first-cohomology ranks, and the first explicit higher-derived obstruction are not computed. Vanishing of the separated compact term does not mean continuous H2 vanishes: the nonzero Jannsen kernel persists. Existence of a full or metabelian section is asserted only where an actual section or a separately proved lifting theorem supplies it.

The next compact-term frontier has globally independent Kummer coordinates but only one residual away-five inertia direction. The global translation subgroup is then smaller than the full two-variable group; its coinduced invariant coefficient is nonconstant. The new formal-coordinate observation in the research notes does not yet establish a Gamma-equivariant cohomology comparison. No new statement is registered for it.

# Checkpoint15 D/E research progress

The new integrated results D86–D89 directly advance original TaskD5, the requested actual metabelian Alexander cohomology and section-fibre calculation.

D86 exhibits and computes an infinite compact five-torsion localization kernel in an actual cusp family; its finite-support parameter26 supplies a genuine section. D87 proves the exact operator-image formula for the entire finite-localization term for every completed Kummer pair. Its compactness argument supplies one finite coefficient level for each class and therefore closes the previously essential finite-level uniformity gate, rather than merely renaming the unrestricted local kernel.

D88 computes the complete compact kernel for every nonzero zero-five-valuation cusp parameter, including arbitrary global divisibility, infinite ramification and the actual infinite local-index endpoint. It retains the nonprimitive boundary torsion, proves the snake map zero and uses transfer to control the whole exponent. D89 handles every primitive-five-valuation cusp parameter with the actual valuation graph, proving a literal zero invariant map and eliminating the extra free local factor. These include actual rational tangent examples and preserve the distinction between H1 fibre translation and H2 compact torsion.

All four integrated proofs passed root and independent audits; their exact supporting computations and primary-source checks are retained. D90 is notes-only: it proposes the next nonunit-valuation range with additional smaller finite cyclic factors, supported by exact integral boundary matrices, and awaits complete audits. It is not included as a proved result in the current paper.

Remaining barriers are explicit: the whole abstract compact-group classification for every dependent Kummer pair, unrestricted infinitely ramified H1 ranks, explicit least higher-derived obstruction stages/cocycles, and the full higher nonmetabelian induced Fermat tower. No generic section existence is inferred from module computations. The original full tasks remain Open wherever these scopes are required.

### de_checkpoint16_progress

# Checkpoint16 D/E research progress

D90--D92 are integrated with full independent audits and retained exact executions. D91 completes the compact separated-kernel calculation on all three cusp packets, including every finite cyclic factor and infinite endpoint; D92 determines the exact section abelian image on the full rational-rank-at-most-one locus and its three ordinary rational-point images. Arbitrary other pair existence, infinite-ramification H1 ranks, and explicit first higher-derived obstructions remain open.

All 15 assigned final PDF page images were actually viewed and passed. DE also completed full independent source/proof audits of C47, C48, A78 and A79. C48 is notes-only for this checkpoint.

The next notes-only exploration concerns global lattice L=5^r Z5 times Z5, zero five-valuation, and local vector (5^N,-1), N>=r. The actual one-variable reduction gives a candidate boundary operator (1+t^(5^r))(1+t)^3 times substitution t->t^2 on Z5[C_(5^N)]. ### de_hoshi_tsujimura_audit

# The infinity cusp in the June 2021 Hoshi–Tsujimura preprint

## Source and exact scope of this check

Verified primary source: Yuichiro Hoshi and Shota Tsujimura, *Construction of Abundant Explicit Nongeometric Pro-p Galois Sections of Punctured Projective Lines*, RIMS preprint 1950, June 2021:

https://www.kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~yuichiro/rims1950.pdf

The source was opened in full, including Theorem A on printed pages 2–3, Proposition 1.4(ii) on printed page 6, and Corollary 2.5 and Remark 2.5.1 on printed pages 10–11. Retrieval references: turn515view0, turn515view1; page screenshots: turn516view0, turn516view1. The observation below concerns exactly that version. No statement about another version is inferred.

None of D.1–D.52, or of Part E, uses this preprint as an input. In particular D.52's abelian slope is (1,2), not a diagonal slope.

## Explicit counterexample to the stated exclusion of all geometric lifts

Take the odd regular prime p=3, F=Q(zeta_3), and x_1=x_2=3. These elements lie in the specified maximal extension unramified outside p and are p-units, as required by Theorem A. They are not roots of unity of order prime to p.

There cannot be roots of unity zeta_1,zeta_2 with

\[
1=3\zeta_1+3\zeta_2.
\]

Otherwise 1/3 would be an algebraic integer. Thus the hypothesis of Theorem A(ii), and all the additional hypotheses of its part (iii), hold.

Nevertheless the pro-p torus section with Kummer coordinates

\[
(\kappa_F(3),\kappa_F(3))
\]

has a geometric cuspidal lift at infinity. Here is the full calculation, including its tangent normalization. On the tripod X=P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}, choose the uniformizer u=1/t at infinity, and take the rational tangent vector a=1/3 in that coordinate. Under the tangential specialization u=a epsilon, the leading terms of the two units defining the torus embedding are

\[
t=a^{-1}\epsilon^{-1},
\qquad
1-t=-a^{-1}\epsilon^{-1}(1-a\epsilon).
\]

The associated tangential Galois section therefore has abelian Kummer coordinates

\[
(\kappa_F(a^{-1}),\kappa_F(-a^{-1}))
 =(\kappa_F(3),\kappa_F(3)).
\]

The second equality uses kappa_F(-1)=0 for odd p. The factor 1-a epsilon has leading unit 1 and contributes no constant Kummer class. This is an actual rational tangential section of the full arithmetic fundamental group, hence also of its geometric pro-p quotient; its image lies in the infinity decomposition subgroup. It contradicts the assertion in Theorem A(iii), repeated in Corollary 2.5(iii), that every lift with these coordinates is nongeometric.

The same example works with every odd regular p and x_1=x_2=p. It is already enough to take p=3.

## The precise missing case and its repair

Proposition 1.4(ii) lists an ordinary point case and the finite punctures a_i, but does not list the puncture at infinity. In its coordinates a_i-t, a tangent at infinity has the same Kummer coordinate at every i. Thus the list requires the additional condition

\[
x_i/x_1\in\bigcap_{n\ge 1}(K^\times)^{p^n}
\quad\text{for every }i.
\]

For a number field or a finite extension of Q_p this infinitely p-divisible subgroup is exactly the group of roots of unity of order prime to p: valuations vanish, and the remaining unit factors have no infinitely p-divisible non-torsion element. For the two-coordinate Theorem A, the sufficient nongeometricity condition is consequently the stated ordinary-point exclusion together with

\[
x_1,\quad x_2,\quad x_1/x_2
\quad\text{all not roots of unity of order prime to }p.
\]

The first two conditions exclude the finite cusp packets, and the third excludes the infinity packet. This is an elementary correction of the cusp exclusion, not a challenge to the separate lifting assertion Theorem A(i), which is not used here.

The claimed examples in Remark 2.5.1 therefore need n_1 distinct from n_2, in addition to both being nonzero, when (x_1,x_2)=(p^{n_1},p^{n_2}). D.52 already uses exactly such a nonperipheral slope.

## Local Kummer construction and actual models

The jet prescription on O(nD) is legitimate by relative Serre vanishing; the prescribed first derivative is a unit, so t has exactly the chosen section as zero divisor in a neighborhood of x. The generic valuation proves the Kummer degree. Completion of its normalization at the unique point over x is literally R[[z]], and remains smooth after every finite coefficient extension. ### fgh

# F, G, H research and verification log

Status: working research return, 15 November 2026. The numbered task rows remain Open wherever the requested general theorem or arithmetic measurement has not been obtained. The additional proved statements are not substitutes for those missing conclusions.

Register correction after checkpoint 01: the current F/G/H JSON has exactly 37 rows, one for each actual numbered statement F.1–F.19, G.1–G.8, H.1–H.10. The 13 earlier duplicate rows labelled only by a lead have been merged into the answers and notes of their numbered statements. The current generator checks exact equality with the statement IDs in the TeX. Earlier checkpoint metadata is superseded by this corrected register.

## Main mathematical progress

**F.** The localic inverse limit is the intersection sublocale. For closed subsets of regular Hausdorff spaces the ordinary limit is the closed subset and the residual limit is empty. For a Hausdorff point germ, arbitrary covering descent has an exact criterion: in every neighbourhood U, the intersection of all clopen neighbourhoods of the point in U must itself be a neighbourhood. This also characterizes whether that point-germ covering category can be the locally constant objects of any Grothendieck topos. For residual germs of closed subsets of regular Hausdorff spaces, comparison with the literal limit holds exactly when the subset is open.

Lead 14 is false in its assertion that locally connected, semilocally simply connected stages always have a replacement topos realizing all covering germs. Discrete tails of the natural numbers give a category with no countable coproduct of its terminal object. Every locally constant category of a Grothendieck topos contains that coproduct, namely the constant countable object. The proof explicitly chooses simultaneous representatives on tails and diagonalizes against the countably many injections. The weaker obstruction that P(N)/Fin is not a complete Boolean algebra is also proved, but is not used to make the stronger conclusion.

A countable surjective tower of discrete groups is a positive case: its prodiscrete limit G has classifying topos BG, and its locally constant objects are exactly the actions with one common open kernel, hence the filtered colimit of the stage action categories. All continuous G-sets are generally a larger category. A compact Cantor subset of the line gives a separate failure of full faithfulness for arbitrary covering descent, despite finite covering descent.

F.19 proves the complementary finite statement without local connectedness: every compact subset of a locally compact Hausdorff space has finite-cover continuity over its neighbourhood germ. The proof extends a finite principal permutation bundle through a finite join model, using an explicit neighbourhood retraction of a finite polyhedron; properness of finite coverings supplies full faithfulness.

Countable intersections of open subspaces of a locally compact Hausdorff space are spatial as localic intersections; F.15 gives a direct compact nested-neighbourhood proof. This proves Lead 21(A) for manifolds. The intrinsic stack formulation is obtained by atlas descent, but the unrestricted torus formula is false: the stack BC2 times a disk retains BC2 in its punctured germ. A geometric point fibre of a representable blow-up and the fibre over a residual gerbe must be distinguished. Closed nested blow-up stages have the stated closed intersection limit. The derived singular-chain calculation is proved with its degree shift and the zero strict limit.

Finite locally constant descent is derived from SGA 4 VI with coherent topoi and coherent transition morphisms. The strict henselian normal-crossings étale limit is identified, its finite fundamental group is the product of r copies of the cyclotomic profinite integers, and it is a classifying topos in local dimension one. In higher dimension a proper nonempty open prevents it from being a classifying topos. Tangential comparison retains arbitrary Z^r-actions on the complex side and finite continuous profinite actions on the étale side.

Lead 17 is proved in the stated complex manifold and number field settings. The cuspidal homotopy fixed point set is a torsor for the completed Kummer group, not merely the rational tangent vectors. The latter embed densely and properly. The finite invariant systems are Mittag-Leffler, so the claimed H1 inverse limit has no lim1 correction. Stix's packet injection is checked with its proper-point injectivity hypothesis.

The literal condition in F.5 is tautological for a hyperbolic étale K(pi,1): every section already defines a homotopy fixed point of the curve. This does not logically refute an equivalence with the section conjecture, which might be true. The claimed identification of all homotopy fixed points with ordinary rational points is false when a rational cusp is present; its cuspidal packet is disjoint from rational-point sections. The actual cuspidal section conjecture is the missing surjectivity statement.

**G.** An independent exact tensor/Lyndon implementation verifies the ambient degree-eight plane. In the prompt's normalization, alpha(A8)=1, nu(A8)=-31/20, alpha(B8)=0, nu(B8)=1. With C8=A8+(31/20)B8, the saturated integral lattice is Z5 C8 plus Z5 B8. B8 vanishes in the free metabelian Lie algebra. Both directions belong to Enriquez's geometric Lie algebra, so every 5-adic scalar satisfies those universal constraints, including the irrational 5-adic square root of 6. This refutes deduction of rationality from those constraints alone, not rationality of the actual arithmetic scalar. The finite nonmetabelian Magnus measurement is specified. G.9 now proves the actual first-coordinate ideal is Z5 and that the actual arithmetic image is saturated in its one-dimensional rational span. Its second coordinate remains unknown.

The Malkin source for the proposed motivic route has now been checked directly. Theorems 11 and 16 concern the Hodge realization. The discussion preceding Lemma 3 explicitly makes the transfer depend on the motivic formalism and hypothetical regulator injectivity. G.8 records this exact source limitation, without concluding that rationality itself is false.

**H.** The attached q2 integral model has been rerun as a standalone program with isolated output filenames, checking 110592 cocycle identities and 2304 projection identities. Over F2 dual numbers, only four of the eight enumerated minimal automorphisms lift, and the dual-number parameter epsilon fails the idempotent condition. Every additive-polynomial automorphism f with f(1)=1 acts compatibly on all abelian Fermat stages, by the integral matrix/cocycle formulas. The example T+epsilon(T^2-T) is nontrivial as a polynomial group scheme automorphism although it is invisible on F2[epsilon]-points; F4[epsilon]-points detect it. A complete class-two Heisenberg calculation shows that the same coordinatewise action cannot extend across a quotient whose commutator pairing is ordinary multiplication. The missing comparison is an integral nonabelian Fermat-stage model at the prime 2. No rational BCH model is silently reduced modulo 2. Actual profinite signed actions are affine linear on all abelian stages, and their joint full-prime kernel is the kernel on the metabelian quotient of the full free subgroup. Individual retained-source images and kernels remain undetermined.

H.9 makes the integral-model obstruction concrete. The rank-five naive Hall class-two scheme cannot carry even the required modular rho action at 2: the verified matrix sends e2 to e1+e4, but the former has square zero and every lift of the latter has nonzero central square e1 wedge e4. All 1024 central lifts were tested. H.10 supplies two smooth integral Heisenberg models with the same rational fibre and designated abelian quotient, whose special fibres have opposite answers to the nonlinear-lift question. Thus the model cannot be recovered from the generic fibre and first stage alone.

The attempted A.2 route does not force cuspidality: a primitive valuation produced by existence can be a Gauss/type-II valuation.

The A.3 proof was independently challenged at the Weil restriction, induced CM type, Kummer image, and splitting steps. No substantive gap was found under the hypotheses written there. The A.4 explicit curve/isogeny/cusp-divisor arguments were also checked; the two genus-one intermediate covers with isomorphic source curves are distinguished by their dual isogeny kernels. The Fermat plane quartic admits no genus-two quotient, since such a quotient would be an unramified involution, whereas a plane involution necessarily has fixed points.

### Completed norm obstruction for the nonstable elliptic projections

Here is the proof behind the preceding tentative norm argument. Put L=Q(zeta3), a=6 or -6, C: v^2=w^7+a w^4+w, F: Y^2=X^3-3X+a, and q_i=(zeta3^i w+zeta3^(-i)/w,v/w^2). The three points q_i(P) lie on one horizontal line, so q_0+q_1+q_2=O. Each q_i maps P_0 and P_infinity to O. Every nonzero integer linear combination q therefore has those same cusp images. The divisor formula for the norm gives div(Norm_q(w))=q_*(2P_0-2P_infinity)=0, so c_q=Norm_q(w) is a constant in L^times.

The reflection j(w,v)=(1/w,-v/w^4) satisfies q_i composed with j = -q_(-i). Hence q composed with j = -bar(q). Norms are unchanged by negating the target when the resulting function is constant, while j^*w=w^-1. It follows that bar(c_q)=c_q^-1.

The discriminants of the defining polynomials, computed exactly, are 3^6(a^2-4)^3 for C and -27(a^2-4) for F. Thus both curves have smooth proper models outside 2,3, with the two cusp sections disjoint there. On such a model div(w)=2P_0-2P_infinity has no vertical component. The map q extends through its homomorphism J_C to F and the Abel--Jacobi map based at P_infinity. The homomorphism remains nonzero on every good special fibre: choose an auxiliary prime different from the residue characteristic, use smooth proper specialization on Tate modules, and the faithfulness of the Tate-module representation of a nonzero abelian-variety homomorphism. Since the image of the Abel--Jacobi curve generates its Jacobian, the extended curve map remains nonconstant. It is consequently finite on each fibre. The relative norm has no vertical divisor, by the pushforward formula for divisors of a norm. Therefore c_q is a unit at every place outside 2,3.

Both primes 2 and 3 have a unique prime above them in L: 2 is inert and 3 ramified. These primes are fixed by conjugation. From c_q bar(c_q)=1 their valuations are zero too. Thus c_q is an algebraic integer unit in the imaginary quadratic field L, and hence a root of unity. In particular the Collino pushforward, whose two norm factors are c_q and c_q, is c_q^2 and has zero rational Kummer class.

This applies to all elliptic quotients in the F-isotypic factor. End(F_overlineQ)=Z by A.32, and the independent maps q_i span Hom(J_C,F) tensor Q, so an arbitrary such quotient becomes an integer combination after composing multiplication by some N. Pushforward through [N] raises a constant to its N^2 power. If that power is torsion, the original constant is torsion. Quotients to elliptic curves isogenous to F are handled by composing with an isogeny and the same degree argument. This proves failure of every elliptic pushforward Kummer detector on the non-CM isotypic factor. It makes no claim that the primitive higher regulator itself is zero.

The S3 representation explains the same limitation: the primitive cycle changes sign under the reflection (which exchanges the Weierstrass points and inverts w), and is invariant under the rotation modulo root-of-unity decomposable cycles. The divisor classes in the non-CM F^2 factor form Sym^2 of the standard two-dimensional multiplicity representation, which has no sign constituent. The missing component is therefore transcendental in this precise correspondence sense.

### fgh_A1_primary_audit

# Independent primary-source check for the main question

15 November 2026, started 10:19 UTC. This note records a check by the F/G/H agent, requested by the root while Part F was in progress.

Opened primary PDF: Shinichi Mochizuki and Shota Tsujimura, *Resolution of Nonsingularities, Point-theoreticity, and Metric-admissibility for p-adic Hyperbolic Curves*, revision March 30, 2024, 107 pages.

URL: https://www.kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~motizuki/Resolution%20of%20Nonsingularities%20for%20Arbitrary%20Hyperbolic%20Curves.pdf

Verified locations: Theorem A (printed p.4); Definition 2.2(i) (printed p.30); Proposition 2.3(v), (ix) (printed pp.37–38); Proposition 2.4(vii) (printed pp.51–52); its proof (printed p.54).

Proposition 2.4(vii) says that for a closed H inside G_K, with H intersection I_K admitting a continuous surjection onto Z_l for some l in Sigma distinct from residue characteristic p, a section H to the geometrically pro-Sigma arithmetic group fixes at most one primitive p-valuation. The open-image hypothesis on the l-adic cyclotomic character appears only in the additional existence clause. Thus it does not obstruct use of a subgroup of an abelianization kernel when a fixed valuation is already supplied by a rational point or cuspidal section.

Its uniqueness proof reduces via RNS to stable center chains, invokes Hoshi–Mochizuki *Topics surrounding the combinatorial anabelian geometry of hyperbolic curves IV: Discreteness and sections*, Corollary 1.15(iv), and then Proposition 2.3(ix). The latter says distinct primitive chains have infinite distance. Corollary 1.15(iv) was opened independently at the author PDF, printed pp.37–41; its global hypothesis asks for open image of H intersection I_K in pro-Sigma-dagger inertia. Cyclotomic fullness is imposed in (iii) for existence, not in (iv) for bounded distance. Taking Sigma-dagger={l} gives precisely the use in MT.

Second primary URL: https://www.kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~motizuki/Combinatorial%20Anabelian%20Topics%20IV.pdf

For a decomposition group D_v=G_{K_v} inside a number-field group G_K, its closed commutator is contained in D_v intersection G_{K^ab}. In the tame local quotient T semidirect hat(Z), the image of these commutators contains (q−1)T, because Frobenius acts on tame inertia T by q. Every l-component l different from p is therefore nonzero and open; projection supplies the required surjection onto an abstract Z_l. The same holds after replacing this subgroup by any open subgroup.

The composite valuation at a chosen lift of a point or cusp is primitive: if A is the horizontal valuation ring, with residue algebraic closure of K_v, let R be the inverse image of its valuation ring. The horizontal maximal ideal is p-divisible and lies in pR. Every prime of R containing p therefore contains that horizontal ideal; the quotient has rank one with radical of (p) equal to its maximal ideal. Also R[1/p]=A, so a geometric automorphism stabilizing R stabilizes the horizontal point. Ordinary-point geometric stabilizer is 1 and cuspidal geometric stabilizer is inertia. This verifies the critical reduction in the supplied ANABELIAN C.7h proof for J=D_v intersection G_{K^ab}, not just the larger cyclotomic kernel.

### fgh_A40_audit

# A.40: all genus-one covers

Status: parent full independent proof/source audit and independent code rerun passed; the parent is integrating the section and row.

## New unbounded algebra

For a proper curve with potentially good reduction, separating its cusps creates a single positive-genus component and attached rational marked trees. Select two distinct cusps P,Q colliding on the good model, root at P, and eliminate Q from the peripheral relation. Write B=k<Omega,t_j, j!=Q>. The actual tree derivation has D(v)=[W,v] for every handle and D(t_j)=[W_j,t_j]. All W and W_j are boundary-linear. Packet changes add lambda ad(t_P).

The Omega coefficients are r=sum m_e E_e(1-Q_e) and c_j=sum m_e j_e(E_e-Q_e). Here r is the strictly positive distance from the P,Q,genus branching point to the genus vertex. Other cusps can be on other trees or on the genus component; then c_j may equal r. Some c_j may be negative. Neither is an obstruction.

The first-core prefix operator is K=D_B+R_W. Its part raising the Omega count is D_c+rR_Omega, with D_c(t_j)=c_j[Omega,t_j]. On a fixed ordered cusp word i_1...i_n, insertion exponents identify its vector space with k[Z_0,...,Z_n]. The operator is multiplication by c_i1 Z0 + sum(c_next-c_prev) Z_h +(r-c_last) Z_n. Its coefficients sum to r, so it is nonzero. This proves injectivity at all degrees, independent of lambda and the signs of c_j. The kernel of the complete derivation is therefore contained in the primitive boundary algebra L(t_j,Omega). All its generators are Tate of weight two, which is exactly the hypothesis of A.38.

The proof does not infer a nonabelian injection from a finite covering map. It uses the actual derived-fixed subgroup and its unipotent closure, not arbitrary rational fixed elements.

## Collision for arbitrary isogeny degree

Let phi:E'→E have degree N. For each p|N, some p-primary kernel point must specialize to zero at some place above p.

* At p=2 or p=3 modulo4, E is potentially supersingular. An isogenous good reduction is supersingular too, so every p-primary kernel point specializes to zero.
* At split p=pi*pi_bar, suppose the p-primary kernel specialized injectively at every place above both CM primes. Prime-to-p torsion also specializes injectively, hence the entire kernel stays distinct and the special isogeny is separable of degree N. The ordinary special [N] map has inseparable degree equal to the p-part p^n. The dual special isogeny consequently has separable degree N/p^n, with no p-primary geometric kernel points. Its generic p-primary kernel T, of order p^n, thus specializes to zero at both CM primes.
* On the target E, endomorphisms [pi] and [pi_bar] extend to the good model. At the pi-prime the first has degree p and zero differential, hence purely inseparable reduction; the second is separable. The formal p^n-torsion is exactly E[pi^n]. The conjugate place gives E[pi_bar^n]. Their intersection is zero by Bezout in Z[i], contradicting |T|=p^n. This proof uses maximal CM only on the fixed target E, so it allows nonmaximal orders on E'.

Translation by any selected cusp turns the zero-specializing kernel point into a second cusp colliding with it. For coefficient prime ell, choose p!=ell dividing N and apply the marked-tree criterion. If no such p exists, the cover has ell-group Galois group and A.22 applies. Degree one is R1.

Every genus-one compactification map is unramified by Riemann–Hurwitz and becomes an isogeny after choosing an origin. A.11 detects any noncuspidal normalized procyclic subgroup in proper H1. For an actual unramified p-torsion lift T, the characteristic-zero divisor gives psi(P+T)/psi(P)=c_T k_T(P)^p. Normalization in the Gauss DVR makes k_T and c_T units. A residue pth root gamma_T of c_T makes g(P+T)/(g(P)k_T(P)gamma_T)=1+p b_T in this unramified DVR. Raising to the pth power gives1 modulo p². Therefore the actual H=(psi−g^p)/(p g^p) transforms modulo p by an additive constant. Its differential descends through the actual separable isogeny.

The descended function f has one pole of orderp and satisfies Df=mu*x. This gives one triple zero and p−3 simple zeros. Their pullbacks are exactly p triple and p(p−3) simple critical points, all away from reduced p-torsion. Since the tail degrees are2 and4, both strictly less thanp, ordinary differentiation detects every potentially dangerous lower Taylor coefficient. The exact charts and genus sum then prove compact type. The p² cusps form p clusters ofp at the remaining main points; every cluster has rational joining paths.

The certificate uses the actual reduced numerator phi_p: its coefficientwise pth root Phi gives x(V)=Phi/g² for the actual Verschiebung. It checks the full elliptic curve identity for y(V), the equation D(Dg/g)=−mu²x(V), and the actual rational pullback equality DH=(D^(p−2)x)∘V. This is substantially stronger than merely checking the numbers of formal roots.

### fgh_A67_isogeny_barrier

# The tetrahedral star does not obey A66's unique-main base-change argument

This is an explicit limitation of the proof, not a counterexample to either cusp assertion.

Let X→E be an A67 tetrahedral cover. Its actual compact-type three-adic model has four elliptic tails, each mapping to the good E model by the same degree3 supersingular isogeny, and a rational centre mapping constantly to O. Thus each tail map is radicial of degree3.

Pull back along a degree-h elliptic isogeny E''→E with (h,3)=1. It is finite étale on good models after finite extension. Each elliptic tail pulls back to one connected elliptic curve: the original degree3 radicial map and the étale degree-h isogeny are linearly disjoint. The rational centre pulls back to h disjoint copies. Every connected tail has one node above each of the h centre copies. The dual graph is therefore the complete bipartite graph K_{4,h}, with

    vertices = 4+h, edges = 4h, first Betti number = 3(h−1).

The proper genus is 1+h(4−1)=3h+1, agreeing with four elliptic components plus graph genus3h−3. For h>1 the Jacobian is not potentially good at this place and this model is not of compact type. The selected cusps still have companions on their rational centre copy, but A42 requires compact type in addition.

In particular a prime-to-six abelian factor cannot be appended to A67 by copying A66's proof. A66 has a unique radicial main component and constant off-main trees; A67 has four nonconstant elliptic components. No fixed-group or normalizer failure is asserted.

## Proof gates checked independently of finite computation

1. Actual curve-to-elliptic map and duplication, actual D_(2m) deck action, four exact cusp indices m/2.
2. Nilpotent ramified-cover theorem supplies only compact type. All automorphisms and endomorphisms are defined after a finite extension, and local automorphisms fix the coefficient DVR.
3. The anti-invariant factor has a unital Q(zeta_m) action, so its actual special étale 2-divisible Tate space has dimension0 or phi(m). The positive case is ordinary.
4. Exchanged positive-genus components are impossible, while components on which sigma acts trivially contribute only to the old factor. For nontrivial components, smooth-curve DS/RH force a genus-zero quotient and minimal different.
5. Ordinary curves have no cyclic4 stabilizer. An order-four root of a hyperelliptic involution necessarily fixes a point over the unique fixed point on P1, so is excluded.
6. Primitive cyclic action forces exactly m/2 ordinary elliptic components in one orbit. A smooth sigma-fixed point lifts by the finite-flat Weierstrass argument to a generic cusp, which is individually mu-fixed; it therefore cannot lie on this nontrivial orbit.
7. The second sigma-fixed point of each elliptic component is a child node. Its unmarked descendant subtree contains positive genus by marked stability. Equal-depth vertices give disjoint subtrees and force genus at leastm, contradictingm−1.
8. Four displayed principal divisors give actual m-primary cusp differences. I=<r²> is the normal Frattini subgroup; HI=G forces an odd rotation and a reflection in H, hence H=G. Norms of functions push points with residue-degree1, and all intermediates inherit good 2-rank-zero Jacobians.

## Historical source ledger (preserved scope)

## Proved dependencies and actual maps

A4 gives the actual 2-isogeny formula from E_(a,b), its coordinates on the fixed E, and the geometric rank-two fundamental group comparison. A70 repeats these maps at every two-power m and independently checks all three polynomial identities in the certificate. Their dual-kernel images are computed directly by reducing t+a+b/t modulo t²+at+b. The stable map is precisely A44's actual cover; the two nonstable intrinsic marked curves satisfy A69. Their distinct dual kernels, rather than source-curve isomorphism classes, distinguish covering kernels over the identity of E.

The only external identity reused is dual-isogeny composition with multiplication by2: **verified:** Silverman, Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves, III.6.1–6.2, primary book https://www.math.ens.psl.eu/~obenoist/refs/Silverman.pdf , previously opened at the exact statements for A62/A64 and used in the independently proved A4. The new all-m generating-pair and Frattini arguments are proved algebraically in the draft. A44 gives potential good rank-zero reduction and actual4m-primary cusp divisors; A41/A42 and A59 give the final fixed and normalizer implications, with their finite-field-extension scope preserved.

## Exact support and limitations

The program verifies the universal degree2 isogeny and kernel translation as rational identities, all three target-E equations and dual kernels, and the three explicit automorphism orbits for m=4,8,16,32,64,128. It treats V4 separately. The proof gives the unbounded argument, so the finite orbit tests are support rather than an extrapolation. Norm maps, residue-degree-one point pushforward, characteristic rotation subgroup and actual intermediate comparisons are all written. This proves only dihedral two-power closures, not arbitrary nilpotent closures or products of two nonabelian Sylow factors.

## Internal inputs and exact scope

- A70 (registered after full root/DE audits) classifies actual dihedral covers of the fixed base. A44/A69 give the potential-good, special2-rank-zero property for every actual central quotient. The n2 quotient is the unramified V4 elliptic isogeny.
- A41 supplies the precise compact-type Abel-map torsion criterion, including endpoints of the rational marked path. A42 supplies the coefficient-equals-residue-prime case. A59 supplies normalizers for nilpotent closures. No pro-prime quotient is used to transfer fixedness.

## New deductions proved directly

1. Every actual generating pair of Q4n has commutator r^(2 odd). Thus the actual inertia is the normal subgroup I=<r²>, with four cusps and genus2n−1. The same elementary group calculation proves I=Phi(G).
2. The central quotient is an actual dihedral cover, and the anti-Prym has dimensionn. The actual deck action r^n=−1 gives a unital Q(zeta2n) action; its local2-adic field has degreen. This controls the actual special étale2-divisible Tate space, not merely Hodge characters.
3. Under the ordinary alternative, exchanged positive-genus components are impossible. Components with trivial involution are retained in the old factor. Exact smooth-curve DS/RH shows every positive anti-component is ordinary with genus-zero involution quotient.
4. Every nontrivial subgroup of Q4n contains the unique involution. Hence a positive anti-component stabilizer acts faithfully. A larger-than-C2 stabilizer has a fourth root of the hyperelliptic involution, excluded on an ordinary curve. Its orbit then has2n positive-genus components, exceeding total anti-dimensionn.
5. The actual quotient C/I is an elliptic V4 isogeny; its kernel is E'[2]. The actual C→C/I map is totally ramified degree n above each kernel point, so actual functions with divisor2(Qi−Qj) pull back to2n(Pi−Pj).
6. Every proper intermediate has at least two cusps by the Frattini property. Actual norm maps preserve good-rank-zero Jacobians and push principal cusp divisors with geometric point coefficient one, giving the exact A41/A42 hypotheses.

## Executed support

notes/fgh_A72_certificate.py checks the exact group law, relations, unique involution, all commutator formulas, generating-pair criteria, subgroup classification, Frattini intersection, cusp counts, intermediate genera, cyclotomic degrees, orbit contradiction and DS/RH equality for eight levels n2 through256. Small levels independently enumerate all subgroups and test generation by every ordered pair. The proof, rather than the finite range, establishes all n. The certificate status and hashes are recorded separately after execution.

## New argument and independent reasoning checks

1. Exact semidihedral multiplication gives commutatorr^((2−n)odd), generatingI=<r²>. All actual generating pairs are covered. Inertia is normal, cuspcount4, genus2n−1; I isFrattini. No arbitrary quotient representation is substituted for the actual covering map.

4. A stabilizer need not act faithfully. Nevertheless any rotation beyondsigma has a fourth-root power whose square acts as nontrivialsigma; every odd outside element is itself such a root. Since mu fixes that root and all cusp vertices, no moving elliptic lies on any root-to-cusp path.
7. Each second fixednode gives a nonempty unmarked child subtree. Equal depth makes all these subtrees pairwise disjoint and excludes every other elliptic-orbit vertex. ## New argument and independent reasoning checks

1. Exact semidihedral multiplication gives commutatorr^((2−n)odd), generatingI=<r²>. All actual generating pairs are covered. Inertia is normal, cuspcount4, genus2n−1; I isFrattini. No arbitrary quotient representation is substituted for the actual covering map.
2. The central quotient is the actual fixed-base dihedral cover. Registered A70 plus A44/A69 gives old rankzero. The actual r^n=−1 action on the anti-Prym gives a unital cyclotomic field of localdegree n, forcing rank0 orordinary.
3. Full component DS/RH handles exchanged components, trivial involution components and nontrivial ones separately. Under the ordinary alternative, every positive anti-component is ordinary with genuszero involution quotient and contributes its entire genus to anti-dimensionn.
4. A stabilizer need not act faithfully. Nevertheless any rotation beyondsigma has a fourth-root power whose square acts as nontrivialsigma; every odd outside element is itself such a root. The ordinary fourth-root obstruction therefore bounds stabilizers by4 without assuming faithfulness. Dimension forces exactlyn ordinary elliptic components in one fullG-orbit.
5. The elementmu=r² is in normal inertia and fixes every generic cusp individually. Its orbit on each elliptic component haslengthn/2>=2. A smoothsigma-fixedpoint would have a finite-flat horizontal lift, necessarily a generic cusp, whose mu-fixed specialization cannot be smooth on a moved component. Thus both elliptic fixedpoints are nodes.
6. Crucial root choice: use the invariant centre of the FULL finiteG-tree, with an abstract midpoint subdivision of an inverted central edge if needed. Rooting only at a mu-fixed cusp is insufficient, becausemu has two elliptic orbits. The fullG-root makes alln elliptic vertices equidistant. Since mu fixes that root and all cusp vertices, no moving elliptic lies on any root-to-cusp path.
7. Each second fixednode gives a nonempty unmarked child subtree. Equal depth makes all these subtrees pairwise disjoint and excludes every other elliptic-orbit vertex. A rational unmarked one-attachment subtree violates stability because its totalvalence2v−1 is less than3v. Thus it contributes positive genus, giving at least2n totalgenus, contradiction.
8. The actual elliptic quotientC/I has kernelE'[2]. Actual totalramificationn pulls back2(Qi−Qj) to2n(Pi−Pj). Every intermediate inherits torsion by norms, good rankzero by Jacobian quotient, and at least2cusps byFrattini. ### fgh_D3_extreme_route

# Actual extreme derivations after A.25

This is a working proof record for the remaining fixed-subgroup problem. The arithmetic occurrence of the two extreme derivations is justified below. The all-degree common-kernel assertion is still open in this return; finite ranks are not a proof of it.

**Subsequent resolution of the arithmetic D3 problem:** A.27, in sections/A_D3_fixed_all.tex, proves the full odd-prime fixed-subgroup assertion using the full separating monodromy and one actual CM Frobenius conjugate. Its all-degree prefix normal form handles the arbitrary based correction lambda ad(Omega). The separate two-extreme-derivation kernel assertion below remains unproved and is not used as an input to A.27.

## Normal arithmetic span

Given an open subgroup Delta0 of Delta, choose a finite number field L/K so that Delta intersect G_L is contained in Delta0 and all maps, cusps, and CM isogenies are defined over L. It is enough to use the smaller normal group Gamma=closure([G_L,G_L]). The actual cusp-packet action of Gamma is IA on the rank-four free pro-l group of D minus its cusp. Its ordinary first Johnson degree is zero by hyperelliptic equivariance. Thus its ordinary degree-two Johnson image is an additive subgroup of special derivations. Its rational span is stable under conjugation by the actual packet image of G_L, because Gamma is normal.

The action on that graded derivation space depends only on the action on H1. After splitting the CM field in the coefficient field, H1 has the characters psi and psi-bar, each twice. An ordinary Frobenius at a split good prime, taken to a suitable positive residue power, has eigenvalues alpha and alpha-bar with disjoint prime-ideal support. They are multiplicatively independent. Its cyclic Zariski closure is therefore the full two-dimensional CM torus. In particular the actual degree-two span is stable under the character projectors. One can alternatively write these projectors as polynomials in a Frobenius on this finite-dimensional space; the ratio of its two eigenvalues has infinite order.

At the place above two of A.25, the local commutator [Frob,tame] lies in Gamma and has nonzero separating monodromy, with scalar (q-1)m. Thus the proper outer degree-two image contains a nonzero multiple of the separating derivation T1 described below.

## Exact comparison of the global CM and local component decompositions

Let the stable components E1,E2 have map degrees 1,2 to the good reduction of the original E, as proved in A.25. Choose a symplectic basis a,b,c,d of their rational homology such that

    f_* a = x,  f_* b = y,  f_* c = x,  f_* d = 2y.

Here x,y is a symplectic CM eigenbasis on E, after the coefficient extension. The degree-two isogeny has symplectic similitude factor two, so this normalization is compatible with the component polarizations.

Adjointness gives f^*x=a+2c and f^*y=b+d. The global original elliptic subspace is therefore spanned by a+2c,b+d; its complementary elliptic subspace, ker f_*, is spanned by a-c,2b-d.

The automorphism rho(t,z)=(-t,-iz) satisfies f rho=[-i] f. The original elliptic differential is dt/z and has rho eigenvalue -i. The complementary differential t dt/z has eigenvalue +i, so rho acts by [i] on the complementary elliptic factor. The component degrees are different, hence rho preserves each component. The two maps f_i intertwine its action with [-i] on the target.

Consequently a global CM symplectic eigenbasis is

    p1 = a+2c,           p2 = (2b-d)/3,
    q1 = (b+d)/3,        q2 = c-a.

The p's have character psi, the q's have character psi-bar, and

    Omega=[a,b]+[c,d]=[p1,q1]+[p2,q2].

The inverse formulas are a=(p1-2q2)/3, c=(p1+q2)/3, b=p2+q1, d=2q1-p2. All formulas are rational; division by three is legitimate even when l=3 because this is a rational graded obstruction, not a proposed integral change of generators.

## Extreme projections and the based ambiguity

Let T1 act by ad([a,b]) on a,b and by zero on c,d. Let T2 act by ad([c,d]) on c,d and by zero on a,b. In the proper surface Lie algebra, T1 and T2 have the same outer class. Direct expansion in the displayed CM basis gives the SAME extreme projections for each:

    weight psi^3 / psi-bar:      (1/9) Dplus,
    weight psi-bar^3 / psi:      (-4/9) Dminus,

where

    Dplus(p1)=Dplus(p2)=0,
    Dplus(q1)=[[p1,p2],p2],
    Dplus(q2)=-[[p1,p2],p1],

and

    Dminus(q1)=Dminus(q2)=0,
    Dminus(p1)=[[q1,q2],q2],
    Dminus(p2)=-[[q1,q2],q1].

Both derivations kill Omega.

There is no silent identification of outer and based derivations here. Every degree-two inner derivation is ad(w) with w in L2(V), whose possible CM characters are psi^2, psi psi-bar, and psi-bar^2. Neither extreme character occurs.

There is also no silent identification of proper and punctured derivations. The kernel of the degree-two map from derivations of the free Lie algebra to derivations of the proper surface Lie algebra has generator values in

    (Omega)_3 = [Omega,V].

It is therefore a submodule of Hom(V, chi V)=End(V) tensor chi, where chi=psi psi-bar. This again has only psi^2, psi psi-bar, and psi-bar^2. Thus the two extreme components lift uniquely from the proper outer derivation to the actual based punctured derivation. Packet changes add a multiple of ad(Omega), of the middle character chi, and do not change either extreme.

It follows that the rational degree-two span of the ACTUAL Gamma action contains both Dplus and Dminus, up to nonzero scalars. No unknown arithmetic coefficient has been assigned.

## Remaining all-degree algebra

The desired statement is

    ker(Dplus) intersect ker(Dminus) = Q_l Omega

in the free Lie algebra on p1,p2,q1,q2. If proved, the first nonzero class of a fixed actual pro-l element is an integral multiple of Omega, by primitivity. Subtracting the corresponding actual cusp power then excludes every remainder and gives the full fixed subgroup I.

Code a_D3_extreme_graded.py checks degrees 1 through 6. In the free Lie algebra its joint kernel dimensions are 0,1,0,0,0,0; in the proper surface Lie quotient they are 0,0,0,0,0,0. Free dimensions are 4,6,20,60,204,670; proper dimensions are 4,5,16,45,144,440. The proper associative reduction uses the one non-overlapping rule p1 q1 = q1 p1 - p2 q2 + q2 p2.

Each individual derivation has many constants; for instance [q1,Dplus(q1)] is killed by Dplus. Thus the incorrect simplification ker Dplus = Lie(p1,p2,Omega) must not be used.

### fgh_checkpoint12_history_review

# Checkpoint 12 history and restoration audit

Status: PASS after the targeted resumed-root metadata fix. Reviewed 2026-11-15 before the 21:40 source freeze. No archive was created by this audit.

## Scope and evidence

I read all four complete scripts: `prepare_final_history.py`, `materialize_checkpoint_history.py`, `restore_checkpoint_history.py`, and `package_compact_checkpoint.py`, including the new current-file-first and external-payload deduplication branches. The materialized index covers checkpoints 01–11: 8,391 historical entries, 1,761 content-addressed objects, 169 exact current restoration dependencies and three individually documented superseded compression encodings. The independent structural check is `notes/fgh_checkpoint12_history_check.json`.

Every snapshot entry has one unique destination. Every object and exact-current reference has matching size/hash metadata, and none of the three decoded replacement destinations collides with an exact historical entry. The historical accounting filename is unused by all original snapshots. I inspected the actual successful restoration logs: checkpoint 09 restored 1,469 exact entries plus two explicitly recorded decoded replacements; checkpoint 11 restored all 1,657 entries exactly. Those complete restoration runs were performed by root, not rerun or claimed as my own execution.

## Inventory and reconstruction

The inventory includes old ZIP metadata as actual historical entries, including entries absent from the old manifest's own list. Materialization verifies each source archive hash and every entry's exact bytes and SHA-256 before accepting a content-addressed object or a current exact dependency. The three omitted encodings are not described as byte-identical old wrappers: their retained full mathematical payloads or exact decoded prefixes have separate byte counts and SHA-256 values. The old ZIP container itself is explicitly not recreated. This is an honest distinction between exact historical files and the three fully accounted serialization substitutions.

The history restorer refuses an existing destination, confines paths within the selected roots, preflights dependencies, follows outer exact-copy aliases with cycle detection, and verifies every copied file. Superseded encodings restore the original mathematical source path; after that, the original historical restore helper skips that existing source and does not require the omitted encoding. The outer restore must run first when transformed raw dependencies are not yet materialized. This order is documented and sufficient; no outside saved ZIP or absolute original workspace path is needed by the actual historical reconstruction.

## Deduplication and the fix

Ordinary operational files are considered before history objects. Every history object is eligible for exact-hash deduplication, irrespective of size. The later pass deduplicates only history objects against verified external stored payloads, preserving operational inputs. Alias chains are flattened and cycles rejected; every final alias points to a literal archive entry. The 169 historical exact-current dependencies are rechecked against their original size and hash at every capture.

I checked the actual current PNG reconstruction manifest: each referenced source PDF is its first ordinary exact-hash representative, hence is literal before image reconstruction. The current paper PDF precedes its duplicate build output. The recipe and decoder scripts remain operational literals. The external payload phase cannot silently replace different ordinary bytes at the same path: a new exact-hash assertion rejects that collision.

One real future-resume issue was found and fixed with root authorization. Extracted root `PACKAGE_MANIFEST.json`, `CHECKPOINT_COMPRESSION_MAP.json`, `ORIGINAL_PACKAGE_MANIFEST.json`, or `RESTORE_LARGE_LOGS.py` could previously enter the hash representative table, even though the writer later regenerates those paths. A historical object could then refer to different bytes after packaging. The capture loop now excludes these four generated names before deduplication, records any present resumed copy's old size/hash/reason in `replaced_root_packaging_metadata`, and explicitly accounts the omission. Payload and literal-source assertions reject collisions with these regenerated names. Historical metadata objects remain untouched and exact. None of the four stale root files exists in the current workspace, so the fix does not remove a current mathematical artifact.

I executed the actual patched capture-loop source against a synthetic resumed root. The test confirms that old root metadata is excluded and its hash recorded, its historical exact object remains literal, the operational PDF remains literal, and its historical duplicate aliases the operational PDF. No archive was created. The result is retained in the independent check JSON. All four scripts parse successfully after the patch.

## Limits

### fgh_compact_type_candidate

# Candidate extension after A.40: compact-type reduction

Superseded research note. The complete proof passed independent root audit and is now registered as A.41 in sections/A_compact_type_fixed.tex. DE separately audited the tensor-intersection and diagonal-conjugacy lemmas. The historical argument below records the development; the registered section is authoritative.

## Proposed criterion

Let X be an affine hyperbolic curve over a number field, with at least two cusps. At a finite place of residue characteristic p, suppose its proper curve has potentially compact-type stable reduction. Suppose the selected cusp P and another cusp Q lie, in the pointed stable model, on a path containing only genus-zero vertices. Then for every ell != p, every cusp packet has fixed subgroup exactly selected inertia under the closed derived Galois subgroup (and hence under the permitted open Delta subgroups in the CM setting).

The condition includes two sections colliding at a point of an unpointed positive-genus component: separation introduces a rational marked tree. It also includes two distinct marks on the same rational component or connected rational subtree. It excludes a path through a positive-genus component.

## 1. The unbounded algebra extends componentwise

Write V=direct sum V_i for the proper homology of the positive-genus components of the compact-type special fibre, with orthogonal symplectic classes Omega_i and Omega=sum Omega_i. Use all cusp letters except Q, each of weight two; handles have weight one. Root the graph at P.

For an edge e let i_e,Q_e,j_e indicate whether genus component i, eliminated cusp Q, and retained cusp j lie downstream. Its boundary is delta_e=sum_i i_e Omega_i+sum_j j_e t_j before eliminating Q. The genuine first weighted derivation, including arbitrary packet lambda ad(t_P), has

    D(v_i)=[W_i,v_i],       D(t_j)=[W_j,t_j],
    W_i=sum_e length(e) i_e delta_e +lambda t_P,
    W_j=sum_e length(e) j_e delta_e +lambda t_P.

The coefficient of Omega_i in W_i is

    r_i=sum_e length(e) i_e(1-Q_e).

This is the distance from the P,Q,i branching point to component i. The assumed genus-free P--Q path makes every r_i strictly positive.

Take B=k<all retained t_j, all Omega_i>. The separate handle-core bases of A.27/A.39 yield a first-core prefix for each core of component type i, with operator K_i=D_B+R_(W_i). Count Omega_i. Its top part is D_(c_i)+r_i R_(Omega_i), where D_(c_i)(Omega_i)=0 and every other B-letter u satisfies D_(c_i)(u)=c_u[Omega_i,u]. The coefficient c_u is just that of Omega_i in the corresponding W_u. Thus exactly the slot-polynomial argument of A.40 applies: on a fixed word of all non-Omega_i letters the polynomial multiplier has coefficients telescoping to r_i. It is injective. The other terms preserve the Omega_i count. Therefore no first core survives, giving

    ker D contained in L(T,U),
    T=span(retained cusp letters), U=span(Omega_i).

This is an all-degree argument, including arbitrary lambda. It is stronger and simpler than separately requiring a generic packet scalar or an explicit CM matrix.

## 2. Exact tensor intersection

The global Galois-stable leading Lie space W of the actual derived-fixed unipotent closure is contained in L(T,U), and hence in every L(T,gU). Here T is globally Tate and the proper quadratic subspace is stable in the weighted graded free Lie algebra.

The free associative algebra generated by T and V tensor V embeds into T(V direct sum T), with V of weight one and T of weight two: a maximal handle string of even length has its unique consecutive pairing, and cusp letters are separately recognizable. Consequently in weight 2m,

    intersection_g (T direct sum gU)^(tensor m)
       = (T direct sum intersection_g gU)^(tensor m).

The tensor-intersection identity is elementary over a field and extends to the infinite family because the intersection of these finite-dimensional subspaces equals a finite subintersection. Intersecting with primitives gives

    intersection_g L(T,gU)=L(T,U_*),  U_*=intersection_g gU.

No freeness of arbitrary surface quotients, no root closure of pro-ell images, and no fixed-point/quotient commutation is being assumed.

## 3. A diagonal symplectic lemma makes U_* Tate

Let G be the Zariski closure of the global action on V; after a finite number-field extension assume G connected. The ambient polarization gives a map from bivectors beta to endomorphisms T_beta using the inverse total symplectic bivector Omega. It sends U to the diagonal algebra of scalar multiples of the mutually orthogonal block projectors V→V_i. For g in G,

    T_(g beta)=chi(g) g T_beta g^(-1).

Thus U_* corresponds, after removing chi, to a conjugation-stable linear subspace of this fixed diagonal algebra. For any element of that subspace, its G-conjugacy orbit remains in the diagonal algebra and preserves its multiset of eigenvalues. There are only finitely many diagonal block-scalar elements with that multiset: each of finitely many fixed blocks receives one of finitely many eigenvalues. The orbit of a connected algebraic group is connected, so this finite orbit is a single point. Therefore G acts on U_* by chi.

This argument uses only the symplectic decomposition, not a CM decomposition or Zariski density theorem. It also works for nonreductive connected G.

It follows that every generator of L(T,U_*) has weight two and character chi. The actual fixed closure satisfies A.38, which proves the proposed criterion.

## Audit questions to resolve before promotion

1. Confirm that the independent handle-core normal form used for several components has exactly the same first-core-prefix behavior as in A.27; inserting boundary letters cannot remove an existing first core.
2. State the compact-type local H1 decomposition and global weighted action precisely: the Omega_i are local symplectic block bivectors, not assumed global endomorphisms. The intersection construction, rather than an arithmetic CM identification, is what makes U_* global.
3. Ensure the graph condition is stated on the pointed stable model after finite extension, and that all finite edge lengths used for r_i are positive.
4. Keep the passage to connected global monodromy compatible with enlarging the field and replacing the derived subgroup by the smaller one. The conclusion for a larger specified Delta group follows by containment and its known trivial action on selected inertia.

If valid, this extends A.40's good-reduction criterion to a large compact-type family relevant to Task A.5. It does not address covers with positive graph Betti number or cases where every path from the selected cusp to another cusp passes through positive genus.
