### fgh_genus2_split_frontier

# The residual genus-two target: exact models and failed component argument

Status: working mathematics after the A54 integration; no additional numbered theorem. The target is

\[
 G:v^2=w^5-1,\qquad G^\circ=G\setminus\{(0,i),(0,-i),\infty\},
\]

defined over the original field Q(i). It is the actual three-cusp quotient in A54 after finite scaling. Its map to the tripod is degree5. This is not an open pro-ell embedding for ell other than5.

## Exact good model at two

Adjoin beta with beta^5=−4. The literal substitutions

\[
 v=i(1+2Y),\qquad w=\beta X
\]

give

\[
 Y^2+Y=X^5.
\]

This has smooth proper genus-two reduction in characteristic2: it is an Artin–Schreier cover of the X-line with its single pole of order5. The three original cusps specialize to (X,Y)=(0,0),(0,1), and infinity, respectively. They remain distinct. The order5 automorphism rotates X and has precisely those three fixed points; the hyperelliptic involution becomes Y→Y+1. Thus the pointed curve is potentially good at2. There is no nonzero semistable monodromy derivation here after the finite extension.

## Exact good model at five

Put pi=zeta5−1, adjoin sqrt(pi), and make the literal substitutions

\[
 w=1+\pi X,\qquad v=\pi^{5/2}Y.
\]

Then

\[
 Y^2=X^5+\frac5\pi X^4+\frac{10}{\pi^2}X^3+
       \frac{10}{\pi^3}X^2+\frac5{\pi^4}X.
\]

The pi-valuations of the nonleading coefficients are respectively3,2,1,0. The cyclotomic equation

\[
 5+10\pi+10\pi^2+5\pi^3+\pi^4=0
\]

gives 5/pi^4≡−1. Hence the special curve is

\[
 Y^2=X^5-X,
\]

which is smooth of genus2; the derivative in X is−1. The order5 automorphism becomes X→X+1, with Y unchanged. Its unique fixed point is infinity. In its Artin–Schreier presentation X^5−X=Y^2, the jump is2, and the wild genus bound is exactly (5−1)(2−1)/2=2. The actual genus attains this bound, so the order argument from A48 cannot rule it out.

Both finite cusps have X=−1/pi and Y=±i/pi^(5/2), so they, and the original infinity cusp, reduce to infinity. A regular parameter there is u=X^2/Y. On the three marked sections its values are −i sqrt(pi), +i sqrt(pi), and0. Their common-radius blowup therefore separates them on a rational component, with three distinct finite marks after scaling by sqrt(pi), and the attaching point at infinity. There is one positive-genus component, the smooth genus-two component above.

The local separating-edge derivation, based on that rational marked component, acts on every proper handle v by m[Omega,v] and fixes the boundary letters, where m>0. An arbitrary selected tangent packet adds an inner term lambda ad(t). Therefore its degree-two value on any proper leading vector is

\[
 [m\Omega+\lambda t,v]\in[v,L_2].
\]

The necessary normalizer equation from A25/A47 has no obstruction at this degree. This is a precise failure of this test, not a construction of a normalized procyclic subgroup.

At every residue prime other than2 and5 the displayed curve and its three marks have good reduction. Thus the available non-coefficient local monodromy gives no additional proper component splitting. The four distinct CM characters over Q(zeta5), conjugated by G_Q(i), all occur on the same genus-two component. Their distinctness does not itself contradict the existence of a normalized line.

## A notes-only fixed-subgroup observation

This observation does not solve the requested split normalizers and has not been registered. Let Delta be the closed commutator kernel for Q(i), and choose a finite normal field L/Q(i) over which the curve, cusps, all CM endomorphisms and a given packet are defined. Put Gamma=G_L intersect Delta, with Gamma contained in the given open Delta subgroup. The proof of the general A38 criterion uses only that Gamma is normal, G_L/Gamma is abelian, and chi(Gamma)=1, so it applies with this Gamma if its Tate-graded hypothesis is verified.

The weight-graded geometric Lie algebra is free on four proper characters psi1,...,psi4 of weight1 and two boundary characters chi of weight2. Polarization gives psi1 psi4=psi2 psi3=chi. Any character in weight d is a monomial eta=psi1^n1 ... psi4^n4 chi^r with n_j,r nonnegative and d=sum n_j+2r.

If eta is trivial on Gamma, it factors through G_L/Gamma and is invariant under conjugation by G_Q(i): for g in G_Q(i), h in G_L, ghg^(−1)h^(−1) lies in Gamma. Since Q(zeta5) intersects Q(i) trivially, the four translates of the primitive CM type {1,2} all occur. Labelled Hodge–Tate comparison forces

\[
 n_1+n_2=n_2+n_4=n_3+n_1=n_4+n_3.
\]

Thus n1=n4 and n2=n3, and the actual character is eta=chi^(n1+n2+r)=chi^(d/2), using the exact polarization identities rather than only its Hodge weights. The proper-plus-boundary graded representation is a direct sum of such characters after scalar extension, so its Gamma-fixed part is pure Tate in every even weight and zero in odd weights. The same holds for the graded closure of the actual fixed subgroup. The proof of A38 would then give full selected inertia at every coefficient prime and packet.

This target is not a cover of the original once-punctured elliptic curve: its simple quartic-CM Jacobian admits no nonconstant map to that elliptic curve. The observation is retained only as an auxiliary comparison; it does not transfer fixed groups backwards through the quotient from the genus51 source and does not exclude an arithmetically normalized line carrying a non-Tate CM character.

# Further Heisenberg covers: exact consequences and remaining gates

Notes only, not a new registered statement. The canonical A61–A62 sources are frozen for checkpoint11. The following even-enlargement argument is an application of their conclusion and the already audited tame model argument; it has not received a separate complete independent audit.

## Every even torsion enlargement

Let p be odd, let C_p be the actual curve z^p=psi_p(x), and take m=2^a m_0 with a≥1 and m_0 odd. Consider the actual finite etale cover

`C_p minus q^{-1}(E[pm]) -> E minus O`, with map `[pm]q`.

At residue2 the elliptic curve has potential good supersingular reduction. Its p-torsion sections remain disjoint. The degree-p cyclic map q is tame, branched only along those sections, so after a finite extension its actual normalization has a smooth proper model and retains q. Write n=pm_0. All generic E[2^a n] points over one reduced E[n] point form a group of size4^a.

At a target reduction outside E[p], the special q-fibre has p distinct etale points. Each receives exactly4^a marked sections, by the actual local etale sections. At a target reduction in E[p], its one ramified source point receives exactly `1+p(4^a−1)` marks: one from the original ramified p-torsion target, and p from each of the other4^a−1 targets. Every cluster therefore has at least two marks. Marked separation puts each cluster on a rational tree attached to the smooth proper source. The hypotheses of A42 hold at every chosen mark, for every coefficient prime and packet.

Normalizer recognition passes from the original affine C_p to this further puncturing by A11: a proposed noncuspidal normalized pro-prime cyclic subgroup has nonzero proper homology. The open immersion has the same proper compactification, so the image remains nonzero and infinite in the original curve, where A61–A62 force it peripheral, contradicting its nonzero proper homology. This argument does not require the enlarged cover's Galois closure itself to be nilpotent.

This gives a concrete extension beyond the original marked sets, but A53 already supplies infinitely many enlargements on every compactification. It is not currently being registered as a separate main-task advance.

## Odd enlargements require a separate critical-centre check

The residue-p models of A61–A62 have positive-genus tails over the zeros of the actual critical function. Extra odd-order torsion marks can only be treated by the same rational-cluster argument after verifying that their reduced images avoid these critical centres, or after analyzing the marks on the tails. The special support cannot be inferred just from the original p-torsion case. No all-m enlargement theorem for every p is asserted here.

## Higher prime-power Heisenberg level

The exact characteristic-zero division identity is

`psi_{mn}(P)=psi_m([n]P) psi_n(P)^{m^2}`.

Its divisor and leading Laurent coefficient both give this equality. For n=p^r it supplies actual maps between intermediate Kummer function fields, for example

`w=z^{p^{r−1}}/psi_{p^{r−1}}(P)^p`,

with `w^p=psi_p([p^{r−1}]P)` on `z^{p^r}=psi_{p^r}(P)`.

This identity alone does not give the stable model of the higher-level curve. The upper cyclic extension remains wildly ramified, and neither compact type nor the required rational cusp paths follow from the degree-p model by a fixed-point or quotient argument. A59 supplies the normalizers whenever the actual finite geometric Galois closure is nilpotent, but the all-coefficient fixed subgroup still needs its own geometric comparison. No higher-level fixed-group theorem is promoted from these identities.


### fgh_heisenberg_intermediates_candidate

# Candidate: all intermediate covers of the exponent-p Heisenberg cover

Unregistered; no claim is promoted before full written proof and independent audits. This is separate from A64's torsion enlargement.

## Exact proposed scope

For every odd p, let C_p be the actual A61/A62 cover, G=H_p, Z=centre, q:C_p→E and f=[p]q. Every intermediate affine cover of f should have both all-prime assertions of TaskA5. The only new subgroup case is S≤H_p noncentral of order p. Its compactification D=C_p/S has genus 1+p(p−1)/2, p cusps and degree p² over U. Normalizers already follow from A59; the new claim is fixed inertia.

Every finite two-generated group of exponent p and nilpotency class at most two is a quotient of H_p. If it is nonabelian it is H_p itself. Its characteristic geometric cover is unique: the quotient of the free rank-two profinite group by pth powers and third commutators has order p³ and is H_p. Thus, if the proposed intermediate statement passes, it settles the original fixed-group question on every finite cover whose geometric Galois closure has exponent p and class at most two, after the usual finite arithmetic descent. No cofinality follows.

## Subgroup classification and actual square

If S contains Z, the quotient proper curve is an isogeny quotient of E and A40 applies. If S∩Z=1, its image in G/Z=F_p² is isotropic for the nondegenerate commutator form. Thus S is trivial or has order p. Noncentral S acts freely on the entire generic proper C_p because every generic stabilizer for G is trivial or Z. Therefore C_p→D is unramified degree p, giving the genus formula. The p² original cusps split into free S-orbits of size p, leaving p cusps.

Let T=S̄≤E[p], φ:E→A=E/T, and φ̂:A→E. The equivariance of q under actual deck translations gives q_D:D→A with q_D f_S=φq and degree p. The map to U is φ̂q_D, because φ̂φ=[p]. Its cusp set is the entire inverse image of ker φ̂, and q_D is totally ramified over each of the p points in ker φ̂. All objects become actual over a finite number field.

## Ordinary p: a place where T is étale

For p=1 mod4, write (p)=π·barπ in Z[i]. The two geometric CM lines E[π] and E[barπ] are the respective connected kernels at the two split residue places. T cannot equal both, so choose a place where T meets the connected kernel trivially. Its nonzero points then specialize injectively to the étale subgroup of E[p].

On the actual A62 model, every nonidentity s∈S changes the target point by a nonzero reduced translation. Consequently it fixes no special point or component point; the generic action is also free. The finite constant-group quotient is an étale S-torsor, so it preserves semistability. The p rational marked clusters of A62 lie above the p distinct reduced E[p] points, each contains p marks, and S permutes them freely. A rational companion path inside one cluster maps isomorphically to its quotient copy, and its two marks are not S-equivalent. A42 gives all-prime fixed inertia for every selected cusp.

## Inert p: domination of positive components

At p=3 mod4, both E and A have good supersingular reduction after finite extension. The special φ has degree p and is purely inseparable. Every cusp of D maps to ker φ̂ and specializes to O in A.

J_D is an isogeny factor of J_C: f_{S,*}f_S^*=[p]. Since J_C has potential good reduction by A61, so does J_D (an auxiliary-prime Tate representation is an unramified direct summand). Thus the semistable dual graph of D is a tree.

Use regular semistable models and extend q_D to the good A. A direct extension proof suffices: Liu9.2.7 resolves the rational map by finitely many point blowups; each exceptional P1 maps constantly to the elliptic special fibre. Descend one blowup at a time. The image of the graph is proper and quasi-finite over the normal original surface, hence finite birational and an isomorphism. This proves descent without assuming a Néron mapping property for a nonsmooth source.

Likewise resolve the actual morphism C_p→D by point blowups of the regular source. **Fresh primary:** Liu, Algebraic Geometry and Arithmetic Curves, Theorem9.2.7, printed396–397, PDF412–413, https://rexresearch1.com/GeometryLibrary/AlgebraicGeometryArithmeticCurvesLiu.pdf , opened in `turn1007view0/1`. The added components are rational. The resulting proper map is surjective because its image is closed and contains the entire generic fibre. Every positive-genus component of D is therefore dominated by one of the original positive-genus components of C_p; a rational component cannot dominate a positive-genus smooth projective normalization (Lüroth).

A61 has one elliptic main component, radicial of degree p over E, and all other positive-genus components map constantly to finite critical centres different from O. After φ, those centres remain distinct from O because φ is radicial on the supersingular special fibre. The composite on the source main is radicial, hence its nonconstant factor through D is also radicial. Only that one source component can dominate a component with nonconstant map to A. Thus D has exactly one such main component, with exactly one point above O, and every other positive-genus component maps constantly away from O.

All marked points of D lie over O after specialization. A rational component carrying one has constant map O. Its path to the main cannot pass through a positive-genus component with a different constant image. All such rational branches attach at the unique main point over O; nodalness gives at most one attaching branch, so the O-fibre has one connected rational subtree. If it is absent before marking, separation of the p≥3 cusps inserts a rational tree at that smooth main point. If present, marked sections cannot stay on its main attaching node. Every cusp therefore has a distinct rational companion, giving A42 at every coefficient prime.

## Remaining audit gates

- Explicit source for good reduction of an abelian isogeny factor (existing Serre–Tate/NOS dependency), and compact type from potential good Jacobian.
- Check the model-resolution and graph-image descent proof carefully, especially that exceptional components are only P1 and that proper surjectivity covers every special component.

The separate prime-to-p isogeny pullback C_p×_{E,[n]}E is also promising. Its actual deck group is H_p×E[n], its proper genus is 1+n²p²(p−1)/2, and the étale base change of A61/A62 has one main and n² copies of each attached branch. Rational marked paths lift through the disjoint copies. This has not yet been merged into the candidate scope.


### fgh_modular_two_group_barrier

# The modular two-group: a precise remaining barrier

Status: notes only, unregistered. This is a failure of the current proof method, **not** a counterexample to Task A.5. All-prime normalizers are already covered by A59 because the closure is nilpotent; the fixed-subgroup comparison outside the closure prime is the remaining issue.

Consider the actual finite geometric quotient specified by a generating pair r,s in

\[
M_{4n}=\langle r,s\mid r^{2n}=s^2=1,\ srs^{-1}=r^{n+1}\rangle,
\qquad n\ge4\text{ a power of two}.
\]

The geometric fundamental group of the once-punctured elliptic curve is free profinite of rank two, so this epimorphism defines an actual connected finite geometric Galois cover, descending to a finite number-field extension. No explicit curve equation is presently asserted.

Its commutator is r^(-n)=sigma, the central involution. Thus the actual cusp inertia is I=<sigma> of order two, the cusp count is2n, and Riemann–Hurwitz gives genusn+1. The central quotient has abelian groupC_n×C2 and is an actual elliptic isogeny. Its Jacobian has potential-good supersingular reduction at2. The nilpotent ramified-cover theorem supplies compact type for the full source.

The anti-invariant factor for sigma has dimensionn and a unitalQ(zeta_(2n)) action, so the actual special étale2-divisible Tate space again has rankzero or rankn. The positive alternative is ordinary. The same component DS/RH argument would force all anti-components to be ordinary with genuszero involution quotient. Any component stabilizer cannot contain an element with an order-four power squaring tosigma. Its rotation intersection is therefore{1,sigma}, and the possible stabilizer is at mostV4. The dimension bound permits exactlyn ordinary elliptic components, in one orbit, alongside the old supersingular elliptic contribution.

The crucial distinction from A73 is that the entire generic inertia is only<sigma>. There is no nontrivial subgroup of the rotation group that both moves those elliptic components and fixes every generic cusp. The2n generic cusps can in principle supply the two smoothsigma-fixedpoints on each of then ordinary elliptic components. In that configuration the child subtrees used in A73 need not be unmarked, and the genus count is consistent:

\[
g=n+1=n\text{ ordinary elliptic genera}+1\text{ old elliptic genus}.
\]

This is a permitted combinatorial configuration, not an assertion that it occurs for the actual arithmetic cover. An actual stable-model calculation, another monodromy kernel, or a different arithmetic detection argument is needed to decide these fixed subgroups. In particular no general nilpotent fixed-group theorem follows from A70–A74.

Atn4 this is the order16 modular group, with an actual genus-five Galois cover and eight cusps. Its coefficient2 fixed subgroup is covered by A22, and all normalizers by A59; no conclusion for the full fixed subgroup at coefficient3 is obtained from the current rational-path method. This is not claimed to be the least-degree undecided cover, nor to lie outside every possible future consequence of the existing results.

# Candidate residual cover after A.48

This note records an **unresolved candidate**, not a theorem about its fixed groups or normalizers.

Let H_3 be the Heisenberg group of upper-unitriangular 3 by3 matrices over F_3. It has order27, is generated by x=1+E12 and y=1+E23, and has central commutator z=1+E13 of order3. The geometric free profinite group of U maps onto H_3 by its two handle generators. Its kernel therefore defines an actual connected degree27 geometric Galois cover of U, descending to some finite number field. Boundary inertia is the commutator (up to inverse), hence has order3 in the deck group. The proper compactification has nine cusps and, by Riemann--Hurwitz, genus10: `2g-2=27*(1-1/3)=18`.

The coefficient-three fixed subgroup is covered by A.22, because this geometric Galois closure is a3-group. No all-prime fixed-group or normalizer classification is presently asserted here. In particular the map on pro-prime groups at a different coefficient prime is not to be treated as an inclusion.

A possible next route is to examine the action of the original order-four CM automorphism on the Heisenberg cover and its Jacobian. Its stable reduction, Jacobian decomposition and non-three-prime Galois action have not yet been calculated in this note. The new rational-path criterion requires an actual suitable pointed compact-type model; it must not be assumed from the cover's group alone.

Whenχ−1 is a unit, conjugation byh/(χ−1) belongs toL and takesg to the common complement. The explicitly displayed cocycle conjugation formula correctly transports its primitive, without assuming pointwise invariance of the cocycle.

A continuous cocycle on compactI_s has finite image. The setsU_r, where its value atg is a(g−1)-coboundary in the fixed finite stable moduleD_r, are genuinely clopen: each is a finite union of equality sets of finite-valued continuous functions. They increase and coverI_s by the preceding cyclic argument. Compactness gives one r withU_r=I_s. Continuous selection of a primitive is unnecessary.

The coinduced representative vanishes onL, so it is unramified at every prime where the untwisted action is unramified. The c0 condition makes residual inertia on the chosen finiteD_r nonzero at only finitely many away-five primes. Every remaining local unramified class is killed by its actual Frobenius primitive in that sameD_r. At the finitely many exceptions, D43 plus the exact finite-local Tate-duality/Mittag--Leffler passage of D80 supplies a primitive in some later finite coefficient module. The assumed whole local-at-five triviality supplies one further finite primitive. Taking a maximum preserves all earlier primitives even if the larger module has additional ramification. Thus the class belongs to one finite global localization kernel at every place, with no interchange of a filtered union and an infinite local product.

The resulting natural equality with the whole operator-image local-five restriction kernel is therefore valid at the stated scope. The final invariant quotient is an exact coefficient-sequence formula; it is not claimed to evaluate its isomorphism type for all pairs, prove section existence, or compute a higher-derived obstruction. This audit is complete and does not promote the unnumbered candidate into the frozen paper.


### fgh_post_checkpoint08_frontier

# Notes-only directions after A.51

No statement below is registered. Included sources and registers remain frozen for checkpoint08.

## More punctures on the same Heisenberg curve

Let C and q be the proper genus10 curve and cubic elliptic map of A.50. For m at least1 put X_m=C minus q^{-1}(E[3m]). The composite [3m]q gives an actual finite etale cover of U of degree27m². It has27m²−18 cusps: the nine points above E[3] remain totally ramified, while all9m²−9 other target torsion points have three preimages. The genus remains10, and the Euler characteristic is −27m².

Every map used in A.50 remains an actual map from this smaller affine curve: removing extra points cannot introduce a preimage of a deleted target cusp. The proper Jacobian and its exact elliptic/non-CM decomposition are unchanged. Thus the same proof should give all-prime procyclic normalizer recognition for every X_m. At each of the original nine cusps, the rational joining paths supplied by A.51/A.42 survive separating additional marks, so their full fixed subgroups should remain selected inertia at every coefficient prime. Newly removed cusp packets require their own pointed-path argument. No claim is made that their individual divisor differences are torsion in J_C.

## A concrete residual Heisenberg-five cover

The general odd-prime analogue is the smooth normalization of z^p=psi_p(x) above E:y²=x³−x, where psi_p is its p-division polynomial. Its divisor is the sum of all nonzero E[p] minus(p²−1)O. It is cyclic of degree p over E, totally ramified at all p² torsion points, so the composite [p]q has degree p³, p² cusps, and genus1+p²(p−1)/2.

Translations by E[p] lift because translating the division-polynomial divisor changes it by p² times a torsion-point difference, and p times that difference is principal. The lifts form a central extension of E[p] by mu_p. It is nonabelian because a nontrivial inertia at the single branch point of an elliptic cover is a commutator. Negation [-1] lifts with z fixed. It acts by minus one on E[p] and trivially on the central mu_p; therefore the pth-power homomorphism from E[p] to mu_p equals its own negative and vanishes for odd p. Hence the deck group is the exponent-p Heisenberg group. This gives another direct model of the characteristic class-two exponent-p cover.

For p=5, psi_5(x) is

    5x^12−62x^10−105x^8+300x^6−125x^4+50x²+1.

In s=x² it factors as

    (5s²−2s+1)(s⁴−12s³−26s²+52s+1).

Thus the proper genus is51, there are25 cusps, and the degree is125. A.22 supplies the coefficient-five fixed subgroup. The complete all-prime fixed and normalizer classifications of this particular cover have not been proved in the present work. A.49 provides different complete examples of genus51 and does not identify them with this Heisenberg cover. No least-index assertion among all remaining covers is intended.

Every difference of two branch cusps is killed by p², by pulling back p(T−U) along q. The curve has potentially good reduction away from p: after potential good reduction of E, the p-torsion branches remain disjoint and the cyclic-p normalization is tame. At residue p one must establish the actual pointed reduction; the rational-path criterion cannot be inferred merely from the deck group or the torsion exponent. For p=5 the original elliptic curve is ordinary, so the p-rank-zero argument of A.51 does not apply unchanged.


## Exact wild charts at three (candidate extension, unregistered)

At each finite two-torsion point T=(a,0), a in {0,1,−1}, let delta=3a²−1. Choose eta²=−3, rho⁴=eta, and z0³=f(a), where f=3x⁴−6x²−1. In the actual function field make the polynomial coordinate substitutions

    x=a+rho² U,  y=rho X,  z=z0(1+eta V).

The exact integral affine equations are

    X²=delta U+3a rho² U²+rho⁴ U³,
    z0³(V+eta V²−V³)=2delta U²+4a rho² U³+eta U⁴.

Their reduction eliminates U=X²/delta and gives

    z0³(V−V³)=(2/delta)X⁴.

Thus each chart has a smooth geometrically integral special affine component whose smooth projective completion has Artin–Schreier genus three. This is an algebraic chart, not merely a power-series approximation. In the Jacobian matrix, the first equation has unit U-derivative and the second has unit V-derivative on the special fibre. Its generic function field is exactly K(C). Normal projective compactification and regular resolution therefore preserve this positive-genus component; after first making C semistable, minimal-model factorization and stable contraction cannot remove a positive-genus component. The three charts restrict to distinct base valuations centered at the three finite two-torsion points.

For the main component, choose pi³=3 and z=−1+pi u. The exact equation is

    u³−pi² u²+pi u=x⁴−2x²,  y²=x³−x.

The reduction u³=x⁴+x² is irreducible over k(E), because its right side has nonzero differential (x³−x)dx. Its function field is k(E)^(1/3); its normalization is the Frobenius twist of the supersingular elliptic curve E. Thus the main component has genus one and maps purely inseparably with degree three to E. Together with the three genus-three components this exhausts genus ten. A51 already proves compact type. On a regular semistable model dominating these charts the actual map to the good model of E exists, and every other component is rational. Each genus-three component contracts to its associated nonzero two-torsion point.

For odd m, write 3m=3^h n with n prime to3 and odd, h≥1. E[3m] specializes onto E[n], with 3^(2h) torsion points in every reduction class. None of E[n] is a nonzero two-torsion point. The marked source points over each such reduction class can only lie on the main component or rational subtrees attached to its unique Frobenius preimage. There are 3^(2h+1) source marks in a nonzero class, and 3^(2h+1)−18 in the origin class (at least9). Separating these sections gives a rational marked tree in each class, with no positive-genus vertex on a joining path. A42 would prove the full fixed-inertia theorem at every added cusp and coefficient prime. A50 already gives normalizers for every m. Even m is not covered by this argument because its reduction set contains the three genus-three tail centres.

Primary model support opened: Liu, Algebraic Geometry and Arithmetic Curves, §§8.3.2,9.2.1, Theorem9.3.21, and Stacks Lemma109.24.2 (tag0E97 within tag0E8C), whose proof explicitly resolves and contracts only rational exceptional components. A precise final citation and independent audit are still required before registering the extension.


### fgh_prosolvable_local_audit

# Independent audit of the solvable local draft, Sections 3–5

Auditor: fgh_geometry. Date: 15 November 2026.

Scope: `notes/de_prosolvable_local_draft.tex`, Sections 3–5 and the finite-group closure argument from Section 2 used there. **The result below is a scoped proof audit, not a promotion of the candidate local section theorem.** The parent is checking the fixed-point localization, birational section input, and valuation argument separately.

## Verdict

The solvable-monodromy enhancement in Sections 3–5 passes this independent audit. I found no obstruction to the invariant cyclic gluing, equivariant replacement of branch disks, or realization of the specified finite solvable fields in the specified completion. The one requested clarification—local divisor orders are congruent to +1 and -1 modulo ell rather than necessarily equal to them—has been incorporated by the author.

## Primary sources and existing analytic calculations checked

* ABBR, *Lifting harmonic morphisms I*, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1303.4812: Corollary 6.21, printed p.42; Section 7.2–7.3, printed p.43; Theorem 7.4(2), printed p.44; Theorem 7.7, printed p.45. Opened primary references: turn558view0, turn564view0–3. These identify local automorphisms, define the gluing action, and identify the stabilizer of the chosen gluing data with the automorphism group of the lift.
* Mochizuki–Tsujimura, https://www.kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~motizuki/Resolution%20of%20Nonsingularities%20for%20Arbitrary%20Hyperbolic%20Curves.pdf: Theorem A and the compactified-model formulation in its introduction, printed pp.3–4, independently opened as turn567view0. The set Sigma={p,ell} satisfies the stated size and containment hypotheses. Its finite geometric quotients are solvable by Burnside's theorem. The parent's separate source audit covers the exact Proposition 2.4(iv) domination statement.
* Supplied local preprint: `03-patching.tex` in full (local normal form, patching, point transfer, horizontal closure); `04-tame-roots.tex` in full through the first-stage construction; `05-arbitrary-roots.tex` in full; `06-realization.tex` in full. The analytic domains and the chosen completed-residue-field embeddings have been checked rather than replaced by assertions about underlying points.

## Section 3: cyclic actions on graph lifts

At a circuit vertex, the cover y^ell=f has local orders congruent to +1 and -1 at its two circuit marks. If the divisor used to construct f meets a mark, changing the Kummer coordinate by an integral base-parameter power removes that multiple of ell without changing the deck character. Thus the two tangent characters are zeta and zeta^{-1}. In one oriented annular coordinate they define the same deck transformation. Every gluing isomorphism between the corresponding monomial annular covers intertwines those actions; the gluing torsor is cyclic and commutative. At noncircuit edges the edge orbit is free, so one gluing can be transported around its orbit and closes because the lifted local action has exact order ell. Corollary 6.21 supplies this exact local action, including its group law, by uniqueness.

All other marked fibres are free cyclic orbits. Equivariant matching therefore exists even for chords, edges between circuit vertices, and edges to identity-copy vertices. A loop can first be subdivided as in ABBR Theorem 7.7, inserting u↦u^ell; its two inertia characters remain inverse. The resulting graph is connected and satisfies the componentwise Riemann–Hurwitz equality, so it is a tame covering with no punctures and lifts to an étale cover. Its degree ell and lifted faithful cyclic action make it cyclic Galois.

For a separating edge, each side contains either a cycle or a positive-genus component; otherwise stability contradicts the valence count 2N−1. A graph cyclic cover or a connected torsion-line-bundle cover of that component makes each covered side connected. Equivariantly joining their ell boundary fibres produces a cyclic cover, and every former bridge lift is nonseparating. Further cyclic covers can be combined by fibre products. Their normal closure over the original curve is still an ell-group: over the first Galois cover the closure is a subgroup of a product of conjugate ell-groups, with ell-group quotient.

The entire inverse annulus, including its attached balls, is controlled by the tame lift's inverse-skeleton equality. A pulled-back coordinate has Laurent exponent divisible by ell; its unit factor has a root because ell is prime to p. This proves a root on every full inverse annulus, not merely on the skeleton or one sheet.

The irrational-level collar argument survives the pro-Sigma domination replacement: vertices give rational values, and an invertible analytic function on a disk has constant norm in the rational value group. The complement of the finitely many source node annuli is compact, so avoiding one irrational level gives a whole common collar avoiding that complement. No finiteness of the map of models is asserted or needed.

## Section 4: equivariant patching and auxiliary covers

On each overlap, a root of the branch coordinate splits every local factor. The exterior cover is consequently a trivial G-torsor there, not just a cover with one section. Choosing one sheet and using all its G-translates gives an equivariant trivialization. Branch disks are disjoint, so there is no additional triple-overlap condition. Gluing finite étale algebras retains G and algebraizes over the proper base. A connected component is a torsor under its stabilizer subgroup of G and remains surjective over the connected base; that group is solvable.

If the lower cover has solvable Galois closure, the normal closure of the upper solvable cover is an extension of a subgroup of a product of conjugate solvable groups by a solvable group. This justifies solvable closure at every composition used here. It is not a claim that arbitrary finite covers of solvable degree have solvable closure.

The auxiliary cyclic curve has two rational residual components and ell parallel nodes. The toric Jacobian calculation supplies a character of slope one on each annulus. The division cover is a J[m]-torsor, so its connected components are abelian Galois over the auxiliary curve. Its normal closure over the line is therefore solvable. The period-coset argument is valid on the whole division pullback: after a period representative is fixed, two adjusted local lifts differ by an m-torsion period, and the period lattice is torsion-free. The analytic character roots consequently glue on each clopen period-coset piece. The explicit middle-collar bound then removes the residual unit even when p divides m.

The horizontal ramification bound is separate from residue-characteristic tameness. The horizontal completed field is bar(k)((t)), with algebraically closed characteristic-zero residue field. Its finite extensions are cyclic t^{1/e} extensions. Indices dividing ell are preserved by composita, conjugates, normal closure, normalized pullback, and an étale upper map; these are precisely the operations used.

## Section 5: the specified field, not an abstract copy

In the first stage the new patched étale cover descends from C_p to bar(k), preserving its finite group action. Its function field has solvable Galois closure and hence embeds in the universal solvable étale field L. Its H-valued generic point uses both this embedding and the fixed C_p inclusion. The exterior analytic map transfers the entire valued point, including its completed residue-field embedding, to the original ramified curve. This gives a K_0-embedding F→H, not just an analytic point above the chosen base point.

Because F/K_0 is normal and E already contains its specified copy, every image of a primitive element lies in that copy of F. Degree equality then makes the embedded image equal to F itself. Thus the conclusion is the literal inclusion F⊂H inside E. It is independent of whether the embedding initially corresponds to a different prolongation of the valuation; once its image equals F, that subfield has the fixed norm inherited from E.

The second-stage auxiliary cover has solvable closure and horizontal indices dividing ell; the patched upper cover is étale and solvable over it. The first stage therefore applies to its normal closure. The same point-transfer argument realizes every finite solvable Galois F/K_0 in H. All such extensions exhaust B. There is no bound on derived length and no assertion that a nonsolvable extension is obtained in this tower.

For the final decomposition-group map in this section, surjectivity uses transitivity on prolongations and compactness, while injectivity uses B⊂H=completion(L): a valuation-preserving automorphism fixing L extends continuously and fixes H, hence fixes B. Normalizing w(p)=1 makes preservation of the valuation ring equivalent to preservation of this rank-one absolute value.

## Boundary of this audit

No global section-conjecture consequence, no bounded-derived-length consequence, and no application through a nonsolvable Legendre cover is approved by this note. Those require the additional arithmetic arguments listed in the draft. Sections 2, 6, and 7 are outside the primary assigned scope here, except for the elementary finite-group closure lemma and comparisons used above.

### fgh_wreath64_frontier

# Actual wreath-order-64 fixed-group frontier (unregistered)

This note constructs an actual next cover. It does **not** assert a fixed-subgroup theorem. A.59 already proves every normalizer assertion for this nilpotent closure, and A.78 proves potential good Jacobian reduction of special two-rank zero. Neither supplies rational companion paths by itself.

## Exact finite group and marked data

Let G=(C2)^4 semidirect C4, with the cyclic group rotating four lamp coordinates. Take a single lamp a and the rotation b. These generate G. The actual commutator [a,b] is the product of two adjacent lamps, of order two. Its normal closure is the augmentation subgroup (C2)^3, which is the derived subgroup. Thus this group is outside the cyclic-derived hypothesis of A.79. It has order64, centreC2, maximal element order8, and no cyclic subgroup of index at most two.

The natural faithful action on four pairs has degree8. The commutator has cycle lengths 2,2,1,1,1,1. Accordingly the full Galois closure has genus17 and32 cusps; the natural degree8 intermediate has genus2 and6 cusps. Its proper map factors as a double cover of a cyclic degree4 elliptic isogeny. The two branch kernel points are adjacent in that cyclic kernel. The other two kernel points each have two unramified preimages.

All of these group/action/cycle statements were checked exactly by `notes/fgh_wreath64_frontier_certificate.py`, with retained `.json/.out`. It verifies all4096 permutation-composition identities, the actual generating pair, commutator and normal closure, centre, Frattini subgroup, point stabilizer, and intermediate ramification. It does not use a numerical rank extrapolation.

## An actual algebraic realization

Work over a finite extension of Q(i) defining the points below. Put

E4: y^2=x^3-6x^2+x, R=(1,2i), T=(0,0).

The point R has order4 and 2R=T. The exact degree2 isogeny to the fixed E:v^2=u^3-u is

u=(x-1)^2/(4x),  v=y(1-x^2)/(8x^2).

Its kernel is {O,T}, and it sends R to (0,0). Composing it with [1+i] on E therefore gives an actual cyclic degree4 isogeny eta:E4→E with kernel K={O,R,T,-R}. These assertions follow directly from the displayed equation and doubling formula; the rational equation identity is independently recorded in the companion map certificate.

Choose Q with 2Q=R. Let ell_Q be the tangent line at Q. The rational function

f=(x-1)/ell_Q

has divisor R+O-2Q. Consequently the actual smooth proper normalization Y of z^2=f is a connected double cover of E4 branched exactly at O and R. It has genus2. Under eta∘q its cusp set is q^{-1}(K), consisting of the two ramified points and four ordinary points; hence six cusps.

For completeness this construction has the asserted full wreath closure, not merely the same branch data. Translate f by K and put f_j(P)=f(P+jR), j=0,1,2,3. If the four square classes had any F2-linear relation, their cyclic F2[C4]-module would have a nonzero annihilator. Every nonzero ideal of F2[C4]=F2[t]/((t+1)^4) contains (t+1)^3=1+t+t^2+t^3. Their product would therefore be a square.

But half the divisor of this product is D_K-D_{Q+K}. Its degree-zero divisor class is -4Q=-2R=T, which is a nonzero two-torsion class. Thus the product is not a square. The four classes are independent. Adjoining all four square roots gives a (C2)^4 cover of E4. Translation by R lifts by cycling those roots, literally with order4; the four root equations have no relation to obstruct this permutation. The full composite over E consequently has group (C2)^4 semidirect C4. Its only branch point is O. This proves the actual cover identification used by the finite certificate.

## What is proved and what remains

A.78 applies to the actual one-point Galois two-group closure at the potential-good supersingular place2. Its Jacobian and every intermediate Jacobian have potential good reduction of special two-rank zero. A.59 proves all normalizer assertions. The full pro2 fixed subgroup also follows from the induced pro2 topology/A.22. The remaining fixed-group question concerns odd coefficient primes and actual marked cusp paths (or a different arithmetic fixed-group argument).

The genus2 double cover has only two possible proper compact-type shapes: a smooth genus2 component, or two elliptic components. If the special degree2 map from a smooth genus2 component to the good elliptic target is separable, its one branch point over the common reduction of K has one preimage, so all six marks lie in that reduction cluster. In a two-elliptic model with component degrees1+1, the generic involution exchanges the components and both branch marks specialize to the node; the actual map again places all six marks there. These cases are promising but are not yet a complete marked-model proof.

The unresolved configuration is component degrees2+0, with the degree2 map on the main supersingular elliptic component radicial and a contracted supersingular elliptic tail over the common kernel reduction. The involution is trivial on the main component and nontrivial on the tail. Its unique special fixed point on the tail is the node, so the two ramified cusps cannot lie smoothly on the tail. The four unramified cusps could still lie smoothly there in exchanged pairs. Rank zero alone does not exclude this, and no companion path is asserted for them.

The actual cyclic kernel has two closer pairs {O,T} and {R,-R}; an exact two-adic chart or a direct Prym torsion calculation is needed to locate the four ordinary marks. Formal-distance intuition alone is insufficient. This note retains that precise missing step.

## Metabelian arithmetic-normal quotient: C32 proof to draft after checkpoint06
Let G_M be the compact actual normalized metabelian image of full GT0, and U its multiplier-one kernel. B7 gives a faithful embedding of U in the commutative unit group via its actual action on Mprime, so U is abelian. This is faithful on actual normalized automorphisms: beta determines the unique conjugator exponent because (X-1)(Y-1) is regular, and B7's normalization is a group section. For c=(-1,1), the normalized coefficient B_c is1 (the entire commutator coefficient is X^-1 Y^-1). C30's all-multiplier crossed law therefore gives B_{cuc^-1}=B_u(X^-1,Y^-1), and B17 gives this equal to B_u^-1 for every u in U. Faithfulness consequently gives cuc^-1=u^-1 as an equality in G_M.

For H equal to the Galois image or the pentagon group, H has surjective multiplier and contains c. Every class of G_M modulo the closed normal closure of its H-image is represented by U; this quotient is therefore abelian. Killing c imposes u=u^-1, so the whole quotient has exponent2. Every C30 vartheta_p factors through this actual metabelian image, vanishes on H, and remains independent by the same full u_p witnesses. Its character rank is at least countably infinite and at most countable by second countability. Thus the entire metabelian arithmetic-normal (or pentagon-normal) quotient is topologically a countable product of C2, not merely its maximal elementary-two quotient. The assertion is restricted to G_M; the quotient arising from the kernel of the full metabelian action remains unresolved. The four valuation inequalities give the fractional-part differential formula. The resulting dimensions (0,1,1,1,1,1,1,2) contain both a balanced embedding and an unbalanced conjugate pair. Thus no balanced-determinant or quaternion conclusion is used.

The maximal CM sub-Hodge structure is functorial under all endomorphisms, hence K-stable. A proper nonzero CM part would have K-rank one, and its quotient would also have K-rank one with faithful unital K-action. If all of B8 were CM, the K-linear Hodge endomorphism algebra has K-dimension at least two by the torus representation. It already contains the persistent quadratic field L_q and is therefore EQUAL to L_q as a GLOBAL K-algebra. The specialized Hodge algebra has the same dimension and must equal it at both places, contradicting the globally distinct square classes. The CM type {1,2} has trivial stabilizer. Labelled Hodge--Tate weights at all embeddings force its four Galois characters to remain pairwise distinct on every open global subgroup. A Q_ell-line in any power of this CM factor would require one character to be invariant along a full local coefficient-field orbit. The no-CM factor has no potentially stable rational line by the stated Ruppert input. ## Algebraic and reduction checks

The map factors as the cyclic degree-m/2 extraction of `y/(x-1)` followed
by elliptic duplication, so its degree is 2m. The divisor at the four
two-torsion points gives precisely the stated four cusp indices. The two
displayed deck transformations preserve both target coordinates and give
the entire dihedral group. The base m=2 is the unramified elliptic isogeny
case. The symbolic certificate independently checks all coordinate and
duplication identities, not just the curve equations.

The odd differential indices give the primitive cyclotomic factor A_m
with dimension m/2 and a unital action of Q(zeta_m). Its completion at two
is a field of degree m/2. After potential good reduction, that field acts
on the actual rational étale Tate space of the special two-divisible group.
Its dimension is the special two-rank, so the only possibilities are zero
and m/2. The latter is genuinely the ordinary case, rather than a Hodge
signature inference.

## Ordinary component argument

1. On a compact-type special fibre the Jacobian is the product of the
   positive-genus component Jacobians. A pair exchanged by sigma has
   isogenous diagonal and anti-diagonal factors. The first has two-rank
   zero by induction, while the second would be ordinary, an impossibility
   for positive dimension. This remains valid for characteristic-two
   isogenies: two-rank is isogeny invariant.
2. For a fixed component B with nontrivial sigma, pullback and norm identify
   its invariant factor with J(B/sigma), whose two-rank is zero. If the
   anti-invariant Prym is ordinary, Deuring--Shafarevich and
   Riemann--Hurwitz give
   `r = g(B/sigma) + (sum different exponents)/2`.
   Each different exponent is at least two. Hence the quotient has genus
   zero and every different exponent is two. A zero-dimensional Prym in
   this nontrivial-action case forces B itself to have genus zero.
3. Subtracting twice Deuring--Shafarevich from Riemann--Hurwitz on an
   ordinary curve gives the displayed sum of nonnegative terms. Thus every
   inertia group has second ramification group zero and is elementary
   abelian. In particular cyclic inertia of order four is impossible.
   If a fourth root of the hyperelliptic involution existed, its induced
   involution on P1 would have one fixed point. An unramified fibre there
   would have two points and cannot support a permutation whose square is
   the deck transposition. The fibre is therefore ramified, producing the
   forbidden order-four inertia. This also covers elliptic B.
4. For an orbit of positive-genus anti-invariant components of length d,
   the stabilizing power mu^d has exact order m/d. A smaller order would
   make a nontrivial mu^k act identically on that nonzero Jacobian factor,
   contradicting invertibility of mu^k-1 in the primitive cyclotomic
   field action. Its quotient action on P1 has order m/(2d), at most two
   in characteristic two. The fourth-root exclusion gives d=m/2.
   The total anti-invariant dimension then forces exactly one such orbit,
   consisting of m/2 ordinary elliptic components. Each has two fixed
   points under sigma.

## Smooth fixed points and the rooted tree

At a smooth special fixed point on a component with nontrivial sigma,
the local action is on R[[t]], fixing R. The series sigma(t)-t has a
nonzero reduction of finite order. Weierstrass preparation therefore
gives a nonempty finite flat horizontal fixed locus, with no vertical
factor. Its generic points specialize to the given point. For these
ordinary elliptic components the degree is two. The only generic fixed
points are the four marked cusps, each individually fixed by mu. A smooth
fixed point on a nontrivially permuted elliptic component is consequently
impossible. The proof correctly makes no such lifting claim at nodes or
on components on which sigma acts trivially.

Root the tree at a marked cusp component, which is mu-fixed. The elliptic
orbit has one common positive depth. The parent edge of each orbit vertex
is sigma-fixed, hence accounts for one of its two fixed points. The other
fixed point must be a different node and hence a child edge. Its descendant
subtree has no marked point: a path from the fixed root to a fixed mark
would force the orbit vertex to be mu-fixed. It has no other orbit vertex,
since all orbit vertices have the same depth. An unmarked finite attached
subtree must contain positive genus, or a rational leaf would violate
stability. These subtrees are disjoint for distinct equal-depth orbit
vertices. The genus sum is therefore at least m/2+m/2=m, contradicting
the actual genus m-1. This proves the induction without presuming a
particular stable graph or silently assuming every component is rational.

## Cusp divisors, intermediates, and final scope

The two function products give connections among all four cusp divisors
with coefficient m. The actual inertia is the normal Frattini subgroup
generated by r squared, so every proper intermediate has at least two
cusps. Its map to E ensures positive genus; its norm Jacobian isogeny
quotient preserves potential good reduction and zero special two-rank.
Pushforward of a geometric point has coefficient one, so the norms retain
the same m-torsion bound on all cusp differences. Their specializations
are zero because a two-rank-zero abelian variety has no nonzero geometric
two-power torsion. The exact hypotheses of A.41 and A.42 are therefore met
for each cusp and a distinct companion. A.59 applies to every actual
intermediate because its geometric Galois closure remains a two-group.

No substantive mathematical correction or scope gap was found. The result
is the stated entire two-power dihedral family and its actual intermediates;
it does not claim a cofinal family or settle the universal cover question.

# B.5: the virtually free realization route — source check

Status: notes only; no new theorem registered. Checked 2026-11-15 at approximately 23:38 UTC during the checkpoint-14 canonical freeze.

## Opened primary source

P. A. Zalesskii, *On virtually projective groups*, J. reine angew. Math. 572 (2004), 97–110, author-hosted published PDF: https://mat.unb.br/pz/arquivos/virproj.pdf . The introduction on printed p.97 explicitly distinguishes the full profinite category from the pro-p category: a virtually free profinite group need not act on a profinite tree. Its example is the semidirect product of the profinite integers by an involution which negates the 2-component and fixes the other prime components. Theorem 2.5, printed p.108, proves only that the quotient of a virtually projective group by the closed normal subgroup generated by its torsion is projective. It does not give the three-reflection presentation required in B.5.

Herfort–Zalesskii, *Virtually free pro-p groups*, Publications Mathématiques de l’IHÉS 118 (2013), 193–211, DOI 10.1007/s10240-013-0051-4, publisher/archive record https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_2013__118__193_0/ . For an actual negative peripheral involution alpha, the group F semidirect C2 is virtually free profinite. This fact alone does not justify treating it as the profinite completion of a discrete graph of finite groups. The generation criterion already recorded in Part B therefore remains a genuine additional gate. The counterexample above does not refute that criterion or the desired conclusion in the peripheral rank-two case: it has a different action. It prevents importing an unrestricted full-profinite realization theorem from the pro-p statements.

Next useful attack: establish a realization theorem with the actual peripheral marking, or construct the three sections and prove their full finite-quotient generation directly. ### pbc_C31_modular_gate

# C.31: exact modular gate for the original source presentation

Status on 2026-11-15 at 18:03 UTC: **comparison lemma proved; computational certificate still pending**. Parent independently approved the comparison before execution. No C.31 full-lift assertion follows until the original source rows and returned correction are replayed.

## The faithful torsion comparison

Let `F_n -> G` be the actual finite source presentation, with kernel `R`. Put

\[
H=F_n/[F_n,R],\qquad K=R/[F_n,R],\qquad N=|G|.
\]

Here `K` is a finitely generated central abelian subgroup of `H`. The integral Hopf exact sequence gives

\[
0\longrightarrow H_2(G,\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow K
\longrightarrow (F_n)_{\mathrm{ab}}
\longrightarrow G_{\mathrm{ab}}\longrightarrow0.
\]

Consequently `K intersect H' = tors(K) = H_2(G,Z)`. The positive-degree homology of a finite group is killed by its order: restriction/transfer through the trivial subgroup has composite multiplication by `N`, whereas that subgroup has zero positive homology. Thus `N tors(K)=0`.

The map `tors(K) -> K/NK` is injective. Indeed, if `Nk` belongs to `tors(K)`, its image in the free abelian group `(F_n)_ab` is zero. Therefore `k` already belongs to the Hopf subgroup `H_2(G,Z)`, and `Nk=0`. No selected splitting of `K`, no rationalization, and no asserted presentation of a processed Schur multiplier is used.

It follows that a relation among the target and **genuine centralizer commutators**, established in the original tail presentation modulo `N`, is an integral relation in `H`.

## Why all allowed words lie in the faithful subgroup

Write `a=alpha(s)` and `b=alpha(r)` in the finite group. The retained left peripheral frames are `B_s,B_r`. The three positive-word central differences are

\[
(B_s s)-(a B_s),\quad (B_r r)-(b B_r),\quad (ab)-(sr).
\]

Their sum is the central defect of the two framed images of `s,r` relative to `sr`. Its image in the free abelianization cancels term by term:

\[
([s]-[a])+([r]-[b])+([a]+[b]-[s]-[r])=0.
\]

Thus the target belongs to `K intersect H'`. For each retained finite centralizer element `c`, the original-source difference `(cs)-(sc)` (or `(cr)-(rc)`) is a genuine central commutator and also belongs to `K intersect H'`.

**The rows for `s^2` and `r^3` are excluded from the modular reduction.** They need not lie in Hopf torsion. The implementation retains their two positions only to preserve the established indexing; their correction coefficients must be zero. All actual correction rows are indexed from 3 onwards.

## Exact computational gate

`code/pbc_build_modular_witness.py` builds `pbc_hermite_modular_witness.g` from the unchanged original-source collector. It initializes a diagonal relation `N e_i` for every original central tail, inserts only the allowed centralizer commutator rows, and performs integer Euclidean row reduction with nonleading coefficients represented modulo `N`. The leading representative `N` is retained during Euclidean replacement so that nonunit pivots use the correct gcd with `N`; it is not incorrectly replaced by zero before that step.

The emitted proof DAG consists of original target/commutator leaves, explicit modulus leaves, original source-identity leaves, and exact subtraction/negation operations. A completed claim must satisfy all of the following:

1. Independent DAG expansion verifies the claimed linear identity modulo `N`, with target coefficient 1 and both forbidden power-word coefficients zero.
2. Every used universal source row is recomputed in the original unprocessed presentation. The abelian-suffix exterior rows are checked as the actual class-two bilinear identities, rather than confused with a single raw associativity normal form.
3. The target and allowed correction leaves are recomputed from the original words. The native positive-word collector already reproduces all 1,862 direct original GAP leaves and the combined target of the known C.27 validation case; its checked arithmetic aborts on overflow. This validation is retained separately and does not replace the new source replay.
4. Source hashes, modulus `N=product(relative_orders)`, finite-group provenance, and the resulting actual correction words are retained.

Only then does the faithful Hopf-torsion comparison turn the modular source-row certificate into the required integral centralization identity. The subsequent full gentle lift and both normalized descent evaluations require their own stated argument; they are not inferred merely from a modular matrix calculation.

# C31: a smaller proved homology annihilator

Status: exact structural calculation completed; the C31 target remains OPEN.
No new modular solution or full lift is asserted in this note.

Let G be finite and let A be a normal finite abelian subgroup of exponent r,
with quotient Q. The integral homology Hochschild--Serre spectral sequence
has, in total degree two, subquotients of

H2(Q,Z), H1(Q,A), and H0(Q,H2(A,Z))=H0(Q,wedge²A).

Both of the latter groups are annihilated by r: their chain modules and the
exterior-square module are annihilated by r. If e annihilates H2(Q,Z), the
three-step filtration therefore shows that r²e annihilates H2(G,Z). No
splitting of the group extension or of the homology filtration is used.
Inducting through the derived series shows that

M = product_i exponent(G^(i)/G^(i+1))²

annihilates H2(G,Z). The square on the abelian base factor is unnecessary but
is a valid harmless upper bound. DE independently checked this argument,
including the exact integral spectral-sequence terms.

All homology in this paragraph uses Z_3 coefficients. For a finite group,

three-primary part. A finite normal 2-kernel has zero positive homology with
these coefficients. Its quotient map therefore induces natural isomorphisms
on homology in every degree.

For an elementary abelian 3-kernel A in E with quotient Q, the homology

`E^2_(a,b) = H_a(Q,H_b(A,Z_3)) => H_(a+b)(E,Z_3)`.

In total degree two the terms are H_2(Q,Z_3), H_1(Q,A), and
H_0(Q,wedge^2 A). The last equality is the integral identity
H_2(A,Z)=wedge^2 A, followed by tensoring with Z_3.

For A_18, the last two terms vanish by the explicit calculations. The only
possible outgoing differential from E^2_(2,0) is d_2 to A_Q, which also
vanishes. There is no incoming differential to this bottom-row term, and no
later outgoing differential because its first index would become negative.
Consequently the ACTUAL quotient map induces an isomorphism

`H_2(G_104,Z_3) -> H_2(G_86,Z_3)`.

Combining the normal 2-kernel comparisons gives the natural isomorphism

`H_2(G_176,Z_3) -> H_2(G_26,Z_3)`.

2^13 comparison identifies the latter with H_2(G_4,Z_3).

# Two actual central covers and the remaining two-primary comparison

Status: complete candidate proof with executed exact calculations; independent review requested. C31 remains Open because the fresh G86 quotient relation is not yet proved. Nothing below uses the failed native-collected G86 relation as a mathematical certificate.

## 1. Actual section of the finite group extension

Use C43's actual groups G=G176, Q=G104, A=ker(G→Q)=(C2)^72, and N=ker(Q→G86)=(C3)^18. The original pc source has SHA256 `95fb384593bfaf97d468bbc51f11cd797484a08cb3ec3b954961085b520ffc88`. For i=87,…,104, choose h_i=g_i a_i. Their powers and commutators give linear equations over F2:

\[
(1+M_i+M_i^2)a_i=g_i^3,
\qquad
(M_j-1)a_i+(M_i-1)a_j=d_{ij},
\]

where g_i^{g_j}=g_i d_ij in the actual source, for i>j in N. The file `code/pbc_top_two_section.py` derives these equations directly from every relevant original power/conjugation word. The 12,312 scalar equations have rank1,224 on1,296 variables. A literal solution is retained. Thus the h_i generate a complement H≅N above the normal odd subgroup.

For each of the other86 quotient generators, choose h_j=g_j a_j to normalize H and induce the prescribed conjugation on its quotient. The18 generator conditions give1,296 scalar equations on72 unknowns, of rank72. The retained solutions satisfy every equation.

This produces a section for the ENTIRE Q, not merely its N-subgroup: Schur–Zassenhaus conjugacy shows N_G(H) maps onto Q, and its kernel is C_A(H)=A^N=0. Equivalently the unique lifts normalizing H preserve every quotient relation. An independent standard GAP positive-word replay additionally verifies all104 power relations and all5,356 conjugation relations of Q in the ORIGINAL finite G. The slower attempt to construct inverse collector tables was stopped before any result; its source/output and stop ledger are retained. The completed positive-word replay does not rely on it.

## 2. The two central covers of A

C43's two explicit invariant alternating forms B_1,B_2 are linearly independent in Hom((Λ²A)_Q,C2). Their ranks, recalculated from their literal matrices, are72 and36. Only the first is nondegenerate. We therefore call the resulting groups central class-two covers, and do not call the second an extraspecial group on A72.

Each B has a Q-invariant quadratic refinement q, already retained and checked against all104 original action matrices in `pbc_two_top_certificate.py`. Define a bilinear cocycle c with diagonal c(e_i,e_i)=q(e_i), upper triangular entries c(e_i,e_j)=B(e_i,e_j) for i<j, and lower triangular entries zero. Then

\[
E_q=A\times C_2,\qquad
(v,z)(w,t)=(v+w,z+t+c(v,w))
\]

has commutator form B and square map q. The distinguished central kernel is the displayed C2. Throughout, an automorphism fixes this CHOSEN central C2 kernel; for the degenerate form the whole center is larger and is not asserted to be fixed pointwise.

For a matrix M preserving q, the cocycle difference c(Mv,Mw)+c(v,w) is symmetric with zero diagonal. Let q_M be the quadratic function with that polar form and zero values on basis vectors. Every lift of M has the form

\[
(v,z)\longmapsto (Mv,z+q_M(v)+l(v)),\qquad l\in A^*.
\]

In particular, automorphisms fixing the distinguished central kernel map onto O(q), with kernel A*. Pull back this extension along the ACTUAL Q-action. Because N is odd and (A*)^N=0, averaging and Hochschild–Serre give H²(Q,A*)=0; thus the pullback extension splits. We construct this splitting explicitly instead of inferring numerical values from its mere existence.

## 3. Explicit actual Q-actions

`code/pbc_top_two_cover_actions.py` constructs the lift for each form. First choose l_i for i=87,…,104 so that the lifted N-generators have order3 and commute. The order equations on a basis vector e_k are

\[
l_i(e_k+M_i e_k+M_i^2 e_k)
 =q_{M_i}(M_i e_k)+q_{M_i}(M_i^2 e_k).
\]

The commutation equations are obtained by applying the two composites to e_k. The script retains their full exact derivation and verifies all12,312 equations after solving them; the rank is again1,224. As two automorphisms above the same matrix differ by a linear functional, checking the remaining central discrepancy on all basis vectors checks the full automorphism identity.

For each j≤86, impose α_i α_j=α_j α_(i^j), using the actual original conjugation word for i^j in N. Here products mean right actions in the stated order. The already constructed N-action evaluates that entire word. On each e_k the equation for the unknown l_j is

\[
l_j(M_i e_k+e_k)
 =q_{M_j}(M_i e_k)+l_i(e_k)
  +\bigl(\text{central part of }\alpha_{i^j}(M_j e_k)\bigr).
\]

The script first checks equality of the underlying matrices, then solves and rechecks all scalar equations. Each rank is72. The same normalizer argument in the pullback extension gives a genuine action of all Q on E_q. It is not necessary to assume that N acts faithfully on A: the pullback retains the actual Q-coordinate, so the constructed subgroup projects isomorphically onto N. Its normalizer has kernel (A*)^N=0 and maps onto Q by coprime complement conjugacy.

Consequently each semidirect product E_q⋊Q, with the chosen actual group section from§1, is a central C2 extension of the actual G. These are ordinary finite groups, not a formal degree-two approximation.

Represent elements as a Q-section element followed by an E_q element. If the original generator g_j, j≤104, is lifted as its section generator followed by (a_j,0), multiplication on the right transforms the A-coordinate v and central coordinate z by

\[
v' =M_jv+a_j,
\qquad
z'=z+q_{M_j}(v)+l_j(v)+c(M_jv,a_j).
\]

For j≥105, use the basis vector a_j and M_j=1, q_M=l_j=0. This evaluates every retained original positive word in the ACTUAL central extension. No native raw central normal form is used.

`code/pbc_top_two_cover_values.py` evaluates the three target differences (B_s s)-(aB_s), (B_r r)-(bB_r), and (ab)-(sr), together with every original genuine s- and r-centralizer commutator. ## Vanishing of module homology and cohomology

Since |N| is odd, it is invertible on A. Averaging makes invariants and
coinvariants canonically isomorphic, and makes both invariant and

the actual normal subgroup N in Q. Every coefficient on the second page
vanishes, including degree0, because A_N=A^N=0. Consequently

`H_i(Q,A)=H^i(Q,A)=0` for every i>=0.

In particular H^2(Q,A)=0. The finite extension1->A->G->Q->1, with its
actual conjugation action, is therefore split. This is the usual extension
classification by H^2; it supplies an actual group-homomorphism section
Q->G, not merely a section of an associated graded object. Thus G is
isomorphic to A semidirect Q, though no particular section is chosen here.

## The full two-primary H2 comparison

Use integral2-adic homology. For finite groups this is precisely the
two-primary part of integral homology. The spectral sequence for A in G is

`E^2_(a,b)=H_a(Q,H_b(A,Z2)) => H_(a+b)(G,Z2)`.

In total degree2, E^2_(1,1)=H_1(Q,A)=0, while
E^2_(0,2)=H_0(Q,wedge^2 A)=(C2)^2. The only possible incoming
differentials to E_(0,2) are d2 from E_(2,1) and d3 from E_(3,0).
The first source is H_2(Q,A)=0. The second differential is zero because
the actual section Q->G makes every bottom-row homology class permanent:
the projection H_*(G,Z2)->H_*(Q,Z2) is split surjective, so no bottom-row
class is killed. There are no later incoming differentials and no outgoing
differentials from the left edge.

The bottom term E_(2,0)=H_2(Q,Z2) is likewise permanent. The spectral
sequence filtration therefore gives an exact sequence

`0 -> (C2)^2 -> H_2(G,Z2) -> H_2(Q,Z2) -> 0`.

The same actual section splits this exact sequence. In particular the
kernel is EXACTLY(C2)^2, not just a group killed by2 or a possible quotient
of that group. The map on the right is the natural map from the actual
source quotient. The isomorphism with a direct sum depends on a chosen
section, but the kernel and the exact sequence do not.

Finally the actual quotient Q->G_86 has a normal odd-order kernel N.
Its positive homology with Z2 coefficients vanishes by averaging. Therefore

`H_2(Q,Z2) -> H_2(G_86,Z2)`

is a natural isomorphism. Combining these facts reduces the two-primary
problem to the actual86-generator quotient plus two explicitly retained
binary classes.

## Scope of the boundary corrections

The independent certificate also records that both invariant alternating
forms evaluate to zero on a wedge s(a), for every basis a of A, where s
is the actual generator g2. The function B(a,s(a)) is additive because
s is an involution preserving the alternating form: its cross terms cancel
in characteristic2. Thus it vanishes for every a in A. All norms a+s(a)
lie in the span of the36 retained A-centralizer basis generators.

This means the simple norm-commutator argument does NOT produce the two
missing classes from these boundary corrections. No vanishing of the
original target in the top kernel follows from a quotient calculation.
The executed G86 search is a quotient positive-certificate search; it needs

are exactly its intrinsic subgroups 5^n(H/C).

Closedness gives separation. For completeness, the successive

The quotient R_s is torsion-free, hence L_s is a pure

to L_s. Over the DVR Z5, Smith normal form reduces any

## Actual local cusp conclusion

The Magnus centralizer proof works for every nonzero `b in Z5`, including nonunits. The series `(1+X)^b-1` has nonzero linear coefficient and therefore a formal compositional inverse over `Q5`. Commuting with it forces commutation with `X`. Coefficient comparison eliminates every word containing `Y`, so the centralizer in the formal algebra is `Q5[[X]]`. Evaluating `Y=0` is the actual group retraction to `<x>`; injectivity of the Magnus embedding then identifies the original group element with a power of `x`.

A geometric normalizer of the nonzero closed subgroup `<x^b>` acts on it by a unit exponent. Abelianization forces that exponent to be one, hence the normalizer is `<x>`. The corresponding result for the other two primitive cusp generators follows by a free-basis change.

For an element of the specialized arithmetic group normalizing the section-inertia subgroup, choose the unit tangential lift with the same residue-Galois image. That lift already normalizes the whole cusp subgroup and its closed subgroups. The remaining geometric factor must therefore belong to `<x>`. Hence the specialized section image lies in the cusp decomposition group. The cartesian specialization square pulls this back to the **actual** pro-five local cusp packet. The kernel of specialization is already contained in that packet, so no hidden geometric kernel is lost.

When `a_q != 0`, the exact abelian inertia direction picks the zero cusp. The primitive cusp inclusion makes its local Kummer class equal to the reference class. After combining the geometric and cusp-inertia adjustments, the actual abelian cocycles agree. The conjugator's abelian image is therefore fixed by local Galois. Frobenius multiplies it by `q`, and the torsion-free module has no such invariants because `q-1 != 0`. Thus the conjugator lies in `H=P'`, as required for the actual `H`-coboundary assertion.

When `a_q=0`, a nonzero specialized inertia subgroup would have a nonzero abelian image in one of the three primitive cusp directions, which is impossible. Trivial specialized inertia, together with the cartesian square and the unramified reference section, gives `c(I_q)=1` in the actual group. This proves both local alternatives used later.

### pbc_D80_audit

# Independent full audit of D80

**PASS**, reviewed by pbc_groups on 2026-11-15. The entire written candidate and its exact certificate have been checked. This remains notes-only during the checkpoint12 source freeze.

## Actual arithmetic images with infinite support

The completed Kummer group is the five-adic completion of the free abelian group on rational primes; the sign disappears. Its valuation coordinates form the c0 module, so each residual coefficient level has finite support. With the coordinate at five zero, independence of a,b modulo five implies that two actual inertia vectors away from five have unit determinant. Their pro-five inertia images generate the full translation lattice, and the untwisted action is unramified there. D78's faithful actual operator argument therefore still proves H semidirect I0 without assuming a finite global ramification set.

For every q different from five, log(q^4)/(4 log6) is integral. Multiplying these bounded coefficients by a c0 family gives a convergent nonarchimedean sum independent of order. Thus the displayed local logarithm is well-defined and continuous. The primitive local vector, the integral cocycle gauge, the actual local surjection to I0 and the saturated kappa(6)-image give exactly the stated local line subgroup. All coinduction and restriction-kernel arguments inherited from D79 depend on these actual images, not on bounded support. The geometric boundary permutations also transport the unrestricted coefficient diagrams.

## Strict local compact-to-discrete passage

I reread D43 in full at the point used here. Its vanishing H1(G_q,A_s)=0 applies to every nonzero abelian inertia vector, explicitly whether or not a metabelian lift exists. Thus the argument does not assume the global section whose existence is left open.

The stable quotients W_r are finite. Their local H0 and H1 groups are finite, so the H0 inverse system is Mittag--Leffler. The compact-coefficient exact sequence consequently identifies H1(G_q,A_s) with the full inverse limit of H1(G_q,W_r); no lim1 term remains.

For every finite W_r, local Tate duality is a perfect natural pairing between H1(G_q,W_r) and H1(G_q,W_r^D). Contravariance in coefficients gives precisely the transition maps used in the draft. Pontryagin duality therefore takes the inverse limit to the direct limit. Continuous cohomology of a profinite group with discrete torsion coefficients commutes with this filtered union: each continuous cochain from a compact finite power of the group has finite image and lies in one stage; the same statement applies to a witnessing coboundary. Hence H1(G_q,D) is the dual of the zero inverse limit, so it is zero.

This conclusion means that a given finite-level local class becomes zero at some larger finite level. It gives no simultaneous bound over infinitely many q by itself, and the proof correctly does not make that inference.

## One common finite coefficient module

The exceptional set E consists of the finitely many primes where the inertia vector is nonzero modulo five. At every q outside E and five, both exponents lie in5Z5. In characteristic five the exact identity (1+u)^(5x)=(1+u^5)^x makes the inertia multiplier trivial modulo (5,(u,v)^4). Thus the fixed ten-dimensional module M is unramified there even if the complete Alexander module has nonzero deeper inertia.

The original action and the constant cocycle c are unramified away from five. D78's exact universal constant, linear and cubic primitives apply to every possible actual residual Frobenius tuple in M. Since inertia fixes M, those are primitives for the full local Galois group, not merely for a formal cyclic operator.

At each q in the finite set E, local discrete vanishing provides one finite stage W_(r_q)^D in which c dies. Taking the maximum of these finitely many stages and4 gives a single W_R^D. All primitives already in M remain valid after the coefficient inclusion, including at places where W_R^D is ramified: the same vector still satisfies the same cocycle identity. At five the unit-slope primitive is already in M, and real cohomology vanishes at this odd prime. Therefore the one global class is everywhere locally trivial at this one finite level. No direct limit is interchanged with an infinite product.

The class remains globally nonzero through the actual coinduction isomorphism and primitive raw Soule restriction from D78; inflation from the actual operator image is injective in H1. This supplies exactly the lower bound matching the previously proved F5 upper bound. Positive depth retains the zero restriction-kernel result from D79.

## Compact groups and actual points

Independence modulo five makes a,b,a-b globally primitive. D77's boundary depth calculation and continuous product decomposition then give the displayed compact groups and T_s=0. This does not determine arbitrary unrestricted H1 ranks, the nonseparated group, or section existence.

The explicit CRT construction has t=22 modulo36 and t=-1+5^(d+1) modulo5^(d+2). These give v2(t)=1, v3(1-t)=1, and the opposite two valuations zero, proving global independence by actual inertia. Both entries are units at five. Expanding t^4-1 gives exact valuation d+1, while 1-t=2 modulo25. Since log6 has valuation1, the local alpha has exact valuation d and beta is2 modulo five. The depth is therefore exactly d. The integer is positive and different from0 and1. Its actual ordinary point section supplies nonemptiness, after which the finitely ramified H1 theorem D74 applies. No assertion is made that every point of the much larger metabelian fibre is point-theoretic.

The whole serialized result equals the owner's JSON for every rank1 through30, including the exact CRT congruences, inertia determinant and five-adic valuations. For a boundary prime L, reduction of Lr=fh modulo L in the domain Lambda/(L) proves that L is a nonzero divisor in R whenever f modulo L is nonzero. On the generator P modulo PJ, the actual multiplier contributes chi^2 and the substitution contributes chi^3. When both local coefficients lie in5Z5, every local translation is the identity on the fixed degree-three mod-five module M. The exact local gauge therefore gives the entire untwisted I0 action there.

Global independence makes all of a,b,a-b primitive. 4. Both `x` and `y` annihilate the extra generator. Substitution contributes

   Thus its compact character is exactly `chi^3`, and its Cartier-untwisted
   character is exactly `chi^2`. The actual `chi=2` operator difference is

5. Quotienting by that generator yields precisely D.84's actual rank-one

6. The boundary-depth minimum is unchanged by `5^h nu r`, including exact
